## Open Items

### TASK-214 — Server-side sessions: the browser holds no token (S9, SEC-016)

| Field        | Detail                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**       | TASK-214                                                                                              |
| **Type**     | Security — session token exposure (authentication)                                                    |
| **Severity** | Medium (SEC-016), with one defect found on the way (a promotion's sessions ended in the wrong tenant) |
| **Phase**    | Phase 5                                                                                               |
| **Target**   | v6.0.0 (RC)                                                                                           |
| **Status**   | Fixed on develop (batch 56b, S9 of the sweep)                                                         |
| **Logged**   | 2026-11-12 (register N-30; `docs/SECURITY_DEBT.md` SEC-016; ADR-057)                                  |

Batch 56b, in both repositories (Playform: its TASK-5015). The decision, its alternatives and its
credits are [ADR-057](adr/ADR-057-server-side-sessions.md); the three choices the owner made on
2026-11-12 are recorded there (the server-held token, "option A"; user routes accept only the
cookie session; the session lifetimes).

**What was wrong.** A signed-in browser kept the identity provider's access token in
`localStorage` and sent it as `Authorization: Bearer`. Any script in the page could read it and
use it elsewhere, and a Cognito token from a password sign-in carries the
`aws.cognito.signin.user.admin` scope, so the thief could call Cognito's own user API with it
and go round the app's step-up (SEC-016).

**What it is now.**

- **The session is a server-side record** (`auth_sessions`, migration 070: tenant-owned, forced
  row-level security, through the data layer) and the browser holds one cookie,
  `__Host-pf_session`: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, `Path=/`, no `Domain`; 256 random bits,
  stored only as a SHA-256 (`platform/auth/session.ts`, `session-store.ts`,
  `session-cookie.ts`). No token is in a response body, in storage or in a script-readable
  cookie.
- **The provider's tokens are sealed at rest behind one module**
  (`platform/auth/session-vault.ts`): AES-256-GCM under a key derived from the new
  `SESSION_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, bound to the session's row; `SESSION_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS`
  opens what the old key sealed, so a rotation signs nobody out.
- **Forgery** — three defences, each for what the others do not cover (ADR-057 D4): the cookie's
  `SameSite` and `__Host-`; an origin check on every state-changing API request (`proxy.ts`, and
  again with the session); a per-session token sent back as `x-csrf-token`
  (`platform/auth/api-fetch.ts` sends it). Refused as the new code `auth.csrf_failed` (403).
- **Lifetimes are governed, bounded settings** (safety tier): users 7 days idle / 30 days
  absolute; staff 30 minutes / 12 hours; guests 24 hours. Enforced on the server at each request;
  an expired session's record is ended with why. A staff member is warned two minutes before an
  idle sign-out and can stay signed in without leaving the page
  (`components/auth/SessionIdleWarning.tsx`).
- **The id changes when the authority does, and the session ends when the standing does**: a new
  id at every sign-in (never one presented before it) and at a factor change; sign-out ends the
  record first, then revokes the refresh token; `POST /api/auth/sign-out-everywhere` — on the
  account page (`components/account/SignOutEverywhere.tsx`) — ends every session of the user;
  a password reset, a role change (the console, the command bar, an operator's promotion), a
  suspension or ban, and erasure end every session of the account.
- **The server renews** a session itself (`renewSession`; concurrent requests make one exchange,
  one result is stored — compare-and-set on `token_version`). `/api/auth/refresh` is gone.
- **A user route accepts only the cookie session.** The guards never read `Authorization`; the
  jobs tick's `CRON_SECRET` is the platform's one bearer credential, registered with the page
  proxy's presence check in `client-credential-register.json` (`bearerReaders`). An app's agents
  hold nothing of a user's: ADR-033 gains an addendum with the rule an issuer follows (the
  agent's own credential on its own steps; the user's consent binds the request; the delegation
  token is the agent's credential at use, and the user's standing is judged by the same rules —
  `userStandingRefusal`, exported from the actor guard for that), and AGENT_ARCHITECTURE says so.
  `journey-coverage` counts the journeys' session helper (`sessionFetch`) as a request call.
- **Cognito**: the session's user is read with the administrative key (`AdminGetUser`), sign-out
  everywhere and removing a factor are `AdminUserGlobalSignOut` and `AdminSetUserMFAPreference`,
  and single sign-on stops asking for the admin scope when the key exists. Signing one session
  out revokes its refresh token (`RevokeToken`) and voids what was remembered of the user's
  tokens, as before (review 7 P3) — it no longer presents the user's token to `GlobalSignOut`. The server-held token
  of a password sign-in is used for one purpose, enrolling a TOTP factor — Cognito offers no
  administrative form (SEC-018, the owner's decision); a single sign-on session, whose token no
  longer carries the scope, is told enrolment is its sign-in provider's (`auth.mfa_sso_managed`,
  403 — never an invalid-session answer, which would sign the page out). The IAM policy grows by two actions
  (TENANCY_OPERATIONS §3.3, with a policy-simulator check); without them sign-in works and
  operator readiness reports `sessions` not ready, naming the action.
- **Signed-in users are moved, not signed out**: the page deletes what its storage held, unread,
  and `POST /api/auth/session/migrate` exchanges the legacy httpOnly refresh cookie (MAC-checked
  as before) for a session. The page stays "loading" meanwhile — no sign-in form flashes.

**Found on the way, and fixed.**

- **An operator's promotion ended the new administrator's sessions in the operator's tenant, not
  the account's** (`makeTenantAdmin` runs in the operator's tenant; the sessions are the other
  tenant's rows): the role changed and the old session carried on. It now ends them in the
  account's tenant (`db/tenant-lifecycle.db`, which fails without the fix: "role_changed" expected,
  "live" received).
- **"Sign out everywhere" claimed success whatever the server answered.** The page now signs out
  only when the server did it, and says so when it could not.
- **TENANCY_OPERATIONS said the erasure attestation has no console screen** (it has had one since
  TASK-202) and told operators to copy their access token into a terminal; the agent kill-switch
  runbook did the same. Both now use the console, and — by hand — the signed-in browser itself:
  there is no token to copy.
- **RELEASE_NOTES' deploy paragraph listed migrations to 064** (there are 070) and eleven
  consumer rows.
- The staff idle notice's countdown was a live region read out every second; it is announced once.

- **The page's read of its session was counted per address with the other session routes (30 a
  minute).** Every page load reads `GET /api/auth/session` once — before this task a page read
  its token from storage and asked nothing — so forty signed-in people behind one address would
  have refused each other, and the E2E suite (one address) met the limit. The read has its own
  rule, `AUTH_SESSION_STATUS` (120 a minute), counted for the session the cookie names (its hash)
  and for the address only when it names none; and a first read the server cannot answer for the
  moment is asked again twice (250 ms, 750 ms) before the page shows itself signed out. Found by
  the E2E run on Playform's larger suite.

**Guards (each with self-tests).** `no-client-tokens` (no credential in `localStorage`,
`sessionStorage`, `indexedDB` or `document.cookie`; no token property or bearer in client code;
no route answers one; every cookie the server sets is HttpOnly — with a register of what an app
legitimately keeps); `user-route-credentials` (no production source reads an `Authorization`
header but a registered machine-credential reader); `session-token-confinement` (only the vault
opens a token; each place one can leave it is listed, with why).

**Tests.** `session-hostile` (a stolen id at another tenant; a replayed id after sign-out and
after sign-out everywhere; a fixed id; a cross-site POST without the token, with the wrong one,
with another session's, from another origin; an expired idle and absolute session, staff and
user; a user banned, erased, given another role or deleted at the provider mid-session;
concurrent renewal; a bearer on a user route; a tampered record); `auth-sessions`,
`session-vault`, `session-store` (+ the contract kit on memory and Postgres),
`session-lifetimes`, `session-idle-warning`, `cognito-sessions`, `r17-hostile-signout`,
`api-fetch`, `auth-context`, `account-page`, `proxy`; on Postgres:
`db/session-store.db` (the kit, tenant isolation, the guard with a stolen cross-tenant id),
`db/moderation-account-status.db` (a suspension and a ban end the account's sessions),
`db/permission-cache-invalidation.db` (erasure does), `db/admin-tenant-data.db` and
`db/tenant-lifecycle.db` (a role change does, in the account's tenant); the replay's 070 step
(isolation, shapes, applied twice keeping an operator's value). E2E `e2e/session.spec.ts`:
sign-in through the form and as a guest (no token in the answer, storage or a readable cookie),
a change with and without the session's token and from another origin, sign-out and the replayed
cookie, sign out everywhere from the account page, an idle session expired, and a browser signed
in before ADR-057 moved over. The deploy smoke test and the monkey start cookie sessions as a
browser does; the smoke test fails a deployment whose guest answer carries a token or whose
cookie is script-readable, and the monkey gains invariant I7 (a session's cookie and token from
another origin never change anything).

**Design check**

- **Reach:** every route guard and so every route; the page's auth context and `apiFetch`, so
  every screen; the auth provider interface (Cognito, the mock, the browser provider, the contract
  kit); the page proxy; a new table with its migration, replay step, retention rule, user-data
  and erasure registration; the environment contract (`SESSION_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), the Cognito
  admin action list, operator readiness; the E2E helpers, the smoke test, the monkey, three
  workflows' harness settings; ADR-057 and the operator documents.
- **Races:** concurrent renewal of one session (single flight in a process; compare-and-set across
  processes — exactly one stored, tested on Postgres); a session ended while its renewal is in
  flight (stays ended: a revoked row takes no tokens); sign-in while another session is presented
  (the old one is ended, the new id is always new); two "touches" in one minute (idempotent
  forward-only write).
- **Dependencies down:** the database down → no session can be read: the guards answer
  `service.unavailable`, never "signed out" and never "signed in"; the identity provider down at
  renewal → 503, the session kept; refusing the refresh token → the session ended; the provider
  down at sign-out → the session ended in its record regardless; the administrative key missing
  or under-privileged → sign-in still works (GetUser as before), the two administrative
  operations answer a coded 503 or `providerSignedOut: false`, readiness says which action.
- **Erasure leftovers:** `auth_sessions` is in the platform's deletion manifest and the user-data
  register (by `subject`): erased with the account; ended rows are deleted by the retention job
  after `retention.auth_sessions_days` (45).
- **Screens × responses:** every screen's calls go through `apiFetch`: a 401
  `auth.token_invalid`/`auth.required` marks the page signed out (it goes to sign-in); a 403
  `auth.csrf_failed` re-reads the session's token once and retries — handled in transport, no
  screen shows it; the account page's new section shows the sign-out-everywhere failure; the staff
  idle notice. The route fixtures were regenerated from the real handlers.
- **Journeys touched:** every E2E journey signs in through the one helper
  (`e2e/helpers/session.ts`) — each person once per run: the run keeps its sessions (the test
  double's cookie and forgery token, in the run's own temporary directory), so a worker restarted
  after a failed test joins them instead of signing in again, and the sign-in limit is never
  raised for the harness; `e2e/session.spec.ts` is new; five journey exemptions are removed
  (`/auth`, sign-in, sign-out, guest, the deleted refresh route), none added.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No: a session is its tenant's row under row-level security —
  an id presented at another tenant's address finds nothing (tested through the guard on
  Postgres) — and the one cross-tenant act, an operator's promotion, now ends the promoted
  account's sessions in that account's tenant.

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** the browser ↔ server credential (the cookie), the server ↔ Cognito credential
  (the sealed tokens, the administrative key), and the new `auth_sessions` table.
- **Actors that exist today:** (1) a script running in a signed-in user's page — an XSS, a
  browser extension, a compromised dependency: the actor of SEC-016. It can no longer read or
  carry away a credential; while the page is open it can still make the page's own requests
  (RFC 10017 §5.1.4), which the content-security policy exists to prevent. (2) Another website
  the user visits while signed in: its requests carry no cookie on a cross-site POST, name its
  own origin, and lack the session's token — refused three ways. (3) Someone with a copied
  session id (a shared machine, a proxy log): it works only at its tenant's address, only until
  sign-out, expiry or any revocation, and "sign out everywhere" is the user's remedy. (4) A
  signed-in user of tenant A probing tenant B with their own cookie: no row. (5) A suspended,
  banned or erased user, or a demoted administrator, holding an open session: ended at once.
  (6) Whoever can read the database but not the application's environment: session rows hold a
  hash and ciphertext. Pre-launch there are no external users yet; staff and the owner are the
  accounts that exist, and the staff lifetimes are the short ones.
- **Bypasses:** a bearer header on a user route (not read — tested per route family and by a
  guard); a session id supplied before sign-in (never adopted); a state-changing GET (none
  exists — the route checks); a request with no `Origin` and no `Referer` (allowed only with the
  session's token; a route with no session yet — sign-in, a guest's start — is refused only when
  it names another origin, so a non-browser client can still sign in, which forges nobody's
  session); the forwarded host a client sets (a forging page cannot set it).
- **Forgeries:** a made-up or edited session id (no row); sealed tokens copied between rows (do
  not open: the row's hash is authenticated data); a renewal answering another user (not used);
  a legacy refresh cookie forged or edited (its MAC fails; a renewal naming another user than the
  cookie's is not used); the session's token of one session with another's cookie (refused).
- **Legitimate flows:** sign-in by password, with a second factor, with a new-password challenge,
  by single sign-on, as a guest; many tabs and devices; a link followed from an email while
  signed in (`SameSite=Lax`); a staff member mid-form at the idle limit (warned, continues); the
  jobs tick and an app's agents with their own credentials; a browser signed in before the deploy.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for batch 56b; the owner's three decisions of
  2026-11-12 (ADR-057 D1 `SameSite`, D5, D7, D8).

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** every caller of `requireAuth`, `requireActor`, `requireAdmin`,
  `optionalAuth` and of the removed `accessToken` on their results (the MFA routes, the guest
  route, sign-out); every caller of `apiFetch` and of `useAuth()` (`signOut`, `signOutEverywhere`
  now answers whether it was done, `session`); every implementer of `AuthProvider` (Cognito, the
  mock, the browser provider, the test doubles in the suites) for `renewSession`,
  `signOutEverywhere`, `disableMfa(userId)`, `confirmCurrentFactor(userId, …)`,
  `confirmForgotPassword` → `userId`; every reader of `REFRESH_COOKIE_KEY` and of the Cognito
  admin action list (the contract, the readiness checks, ENV_REFERENCE, TENANCY_OPERATIONS —
  held equal by `cognito-admin-actions`, the policy-simulator command included); every place a
  role, a status or an account's existence changes (searched by `invalidatePermissions` and
  `revokeTokenVerification`, which already marked them); every script and workflow that sent a
  bearer (the E2E specs, the smoke test, the monkey; the k6 scripts send none).
- **Hostile re-read:** the cookie name in a non-production build (`pf_session`, never accepted by
  a production build, which reads only the `__Host-` name); a session row whose `kind` is `guest`
  presented to a user route; lifetimes of 0, negative, NaN or 1e15 in the settings (clamped to
  the bounds); permissions unreadable while choosing an audience (staff limits); `x-csrf-token`
  of the right length and wrong value (constant-time compare); `Origin: null`; an `Origin` that
  only starts with this origin; a sign-out replayed (records and revokes once); a promotion
  across tenants (the defect above); a countdown that reaches zero while "Stay signed in" is in
  flight (the server's answer decides).

### TASK-213 — Batch 56a: the tests' shell proven on macOS (bash 3.2, BSD tools), and the open Dependabot bumps taken on develop

| Field        | Detail                                                                                         |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**       | TASK-213                                                                                       |
| **Type**     | Defect (a commit script failed on the owner's Mac, unseen by every gate); dependency upkeep    |
| **Severity** | Low (T-1); Important (Next 16.4.5's security release; fast-uri's floor); Nit (registers, docs) |
| **Phase**    | Phase 5                                                                                        |
| **Target**   | v6.0.0 (RC)                                                                                    |
| **Status**   | Fixed on develop (batch 56a)                                                                   |
| **Logged**   | 2026-11-12 (register T-1; the open Dependabot pull requests)                                   |

Batch 56a, in both repositories (Playform: its TASK-5014).

**T-1 — a macOS gate.** On 2026-11-10 the 55d commit script failed on the owner's Mac:
`sync-carried-guard.sh` used `case` inside `$( )`, which macOS's bash 3.2 cannot parse (it finds
the end of a command substitution by counting parentheses; bash 4.0 began parsing it). Every gate
ran on Linux. Now:

- `.github/workflows/macos.yml` runs what the owner runs — `npm ci`, then `npm test` with no
  database and no `CI` (`env -u CI npm test`; GitHub sets `CI=true`) — on `macos-26`, pinned as
  every job is (macos-latest's image today: Apple silicon, Bash 3.2.57, per actions/runner-images).
  A step puts `/bin/bash` first on `PATH` as `bash` and fails unless it is 3.2, so no Homebrew bash
  stands in; it prints `bash --version`; the job sets `REQUIRE_BASH_3_2=1`, and the last test of
  `shell-portability` then fails unless the bash the tests start is 3.2. Seed and results as D-16.
  This repository is public, so it runs on every push and pull request to develop, staging and
  main; Playform's runs weekly, on demand and on a change to shell (its TASK-5014: cost).
- `workflow-hygiene` allows exactly `macos-26`, and only in `macos.yml` (anywhere else it is
  refused: macOS minutes are billed at about ten times Linux's on a private repository); D-20 is
  turned around there: the macOS job must not set `REQUIRE_DB_TESTS` or `REQUIRE_VALKEY_TESTS`.
- `__tests__/shell-portability.test.ts` (shared) reads every shell script (`*.sh`, `*.bash`, and
  any file with a bash or sh shebang) and every workflow step a test executes (`EXECUTED_STEPS`,
  by test file), through a lexer that blanks comments, quoted data and here-document bodies, and
  refuses: `case` or a comment inside `$( )`; bash 4+ syntax (`mapfile`/`readarray`, `coproc`,
  `declare -A/-n/-g/-l/-u`, `${x,,}` `${x^^}`, `${x@Q}`, negative subscripts and lengths, `|&`,
  `&>>`, `;;&`/`;&`, `[[ -v ]]`, `wait -n`, `$EPOCHSECONDS`/`$EPOCHREALTIME`/`$BASHPID`/`$SRANDOM`/
  `$BASH_ARGV0`, shopt options 3.2 lacks); a bare `"${a[@]}"` under `set -u` unless every
  assignment gives the array an element; GNU-only options (`sed -i` without a suffix, `grep -P`,
  `date -d`, `readlink -f/-e/-m`, `stat -c`, `sort -V`, `head -n -N`, `xargs -r`, `base64 -w`,
  `find -printf/-regextype`) and GNU tools macOS lacks (`timeout`, `tac`, `nproc`, `stdbuf`,
  `numfmt`). Every test file that runs `bash -c`/`sh -c` with a built string must be listed; a
  literal is scanned where it stands; `execSync`, `exec` and `shell: true` are refused. It also
  holds the macOS workflow to the owner's run, and (where it filters by path) to a trigger for
  every script, shell-running test and executed workflow. Sources: GNU bash NEWS/CHANGES (4.0–5.2),
  Apple's manual pages for each tool, actions/runner-images. It replaces `sync-carried-guard`'s
  narrow "no case statement" test: the class is covered for every script.
- It found one: `scripts/migration-replay.sh` expanded `REAPPLY_EXEMPT=()` bare under `set -u`, so
  bash 3.2 would exit "unbound variable" before the replay's first re-application; now
  `${REAPPLY_EXEMPT[@]+"${REAPPLY_EXEMPT[@]}"}`.
- The rule: CLAUDE.md (standing rules) and REVIEW.md rule 26; ASSURANCE (cadence, §2, §6).

**Dependabot (pull requests open on 2026-11-12), applied on develop by hand:** `ioredis` 5.11.1 →
6.0.0 (#459: RESP3 by default with RESP2-shaped replies, "legacy" mapping; Node ≥ 20; the Valkey
provider's options are all explicit — the cache suites pass against a TLS redis-server 7);
`next` and `eslint-config-next` 16.4.3 → **16.4.5**, not the pull request's 16.4.4 (#468): 16.4.4's
own notes announce the security release published the next day, 16.4.5 (nextjs.org, "November
2026 Security Release": GHSA-mfr8-8qww-v76h High, GHSA-vc7v-qv4w-wrv8, GHSA-rhh4-g77r-r9qj,
GHSA-pc58-hwjq-p385, GHSA-f3mh-rxg3-f5g2, GHSA-7qx7-33qx-rqx2 and one without an id; npm's
advisory database does not list them yet, so `npm audit` stays silent); `jose` 6.2.13 → 6.2.15 and
`eslint-plugin-regexp` 3.3.1 → 3.3.3 (#468); `github/codeql-action` init, autobuild and analyze
4.38.3 → 4.39.1, upload-sarif → 4.39.3 (#464–#467; the SHAs Dependabot pinned). Already on develop:
`@stryker-mutator/core` 10.1.1 (#470), `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` 19.3.0 (#453, #455),
fast-uri 3.1.9 in the lock (#463, against main).

**Found on the way, fixed:** fast-uri's override floor stayed `^3.1.8` while 3.1.9 fixed four
advisories (#463's): now `^3.1.9`. `scripts/override-audit.mjs` checked only that a key had a row,
so the register's Pinned column could say anything: it now requires the row to state the value
`package.json` has (an object as "dep range", a gloss in parentheses allowed) and fails naming
both. The browserslist and `@humanfs/node` rows said "Original advisory to confirm": confirmed
against npm's advisory database (GHSA-c83g-rgw3-j3cx and GHSA-73wf-gq98-2v4g through 4.28.6;
GHSA-p498-v437-472g below 0.16.8). `__tests__/runtime-dependencies.test.ts` (shared): every
production dependency is imported by code that ships, or excepted with a reason that is checked
(`@sentry/nextjs`'s computed require, `react-dom` as next's peer, `@supabase/supabase-js` for
Realtime, ADR-053 §5) — Playform carried `@anthropic-ai/sdk` there unused since March (its
TASK-5014). ASSURANCE said this repository runs no browser E2E (§3, §6): false since TASK-204's
Layer 3; corrected. TASK-096 resolved (Playform's TASK-5014 has the evidence).

**Tests.** `shell-portability` (each refusal planted, with its line; what bash 3.2 and BSD run
passed; a test's shell use classified; executed steps found and scanned; the macOS workflow's
requirements and trigger; the bash version under `REQUIRE_BASH_3_2`); `workflow-hygiene` (the
macOS image only in `macos.yml`; D-20 inverted there); `override-audit` (Pinned disagreements,
object values, a gloss, an app's own row); `runtime-dependencies`; the Valkey suites on ioredis 6
against a real server.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** CI (a new workflow; the runner pin and D-20 in `workflow-hygiene`); two new guards; a
  shell script (`migration-replay.sh`, one line); the override audit and its register; the
  dependencies and lockfile; CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, ASSURANCE, SECURITY_DEBT. No route, screen or
  migration.
- **Races:** none: the guards read files; the workflow runs alone.
- **Dependencies down:** a macOS runner outage fails the macOS check only (not the CI pipeline); the
  Valkey provider on ioredis 6 behaves as before when the server is down (its suites' down cases).
- **Erasure leftovers:** none: no change stores or removes anyone's data.
- **Screens × responses:** no screen or response changes. Next 16.4.5 renders the same pages: the
  E2E specs, base and change, and the pages walked at 1280 and 390 px.
- **Journeys touched:** none changed; E2E spec by spec on both repositories, base and change.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No. Next 16.4.5 closes cross-tenant cache disclosures in
  `use cache` (the platform does not use Cache Components; the patch is taken regardless).

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** the CI workflows (a new job and the guard's rules); the dependency tree that ships.
- **Actors that exist today:** the owner, who pushes and runs every commit script on his Mac; the
  agents preparing those scripts; Dependabot, whose pull requests run CI without secrets. The new
  job reads the code only (`contents: read`, no secret, `persist-credentials: false`). The
  dependency bumps change what every user's request runs through (Next, jose, ioredis).
- **Bypasses:** a script that runs shell another way — refused (`execSync`, `exec`, `shell: true`);
  a shell construct the scan does not know — the macOS job runs it under bash 3.2; a macOS label
  outside `macos.yml`, or `-latest` — refused.
- **Forgeries:** none: no input crosses a trust boundary.
- **Legitimate flows:** the owner's `npm test` on his Mac; CI on Linux unchanged; a Dependabot pull
  request for a version develop already has closes itself.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for batch 56a (2026-11-12): T-1 with Playform's
  triggers decided by the owner, and the open Dependabot pull requests.

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** every test that starts bash or sh (both repositories, `__tests__/**`, the
  helpers and the `.mjs` mutation suite) and every workflow step one runs; every reader of
  `RUNNER_IMAGE` and `jestPassProblems`; every importer of ioredis (`valkey-cache.ts`,
  `valkey-connector.ts`'s `AbstractConnector`, still exported); every reader of the override
  register (the audit, the weekly re-audit); every production dependency's importers.
- **Hostile re-read:** a `case` on the line after `$(` and in double quotes (found); `$( # it's )`
  (found); `<<<` after a loop (a here-string, not a here-document — the lexer once took it for one
  and blanked the rest: fixed, tested); `"$1"` in an array (one element, not flagged); `("$@")`
  (may be empty: flagged); `sed -i ''` (BSD-only: flagged too, since GNU reads `''` as the script);
  `xargs -n 1 sed -i` (the nested command found); a path filter `**/*.sh` against a root file
  (matched); a Pinned cell `$deepmergex` (refused) and `$deepmerge (file:…)` (passed). The scripts
  tests write at run time (two stub `gh`, two stub `git`, stub `curl` and `docker`) were read by hand
  against the list — portable — and the scan now reads them too (a template literal, or a string
  array joined with "\n", that starts with a shell shebang); the stub `git` ran the real git by an
  unquoted path, which a path with a space would split: quoted.
- **After landing (2026-11-13):** CI's workflow lint failed on the push: actionlint 1.7.7, the
  version `ci.yml` pinned, predates the `macos-26` runner label and refused it, while the batch had
  linted with a newer build than CI's. `ci.yml` now pins actionlint 1.7.10 (sha256 from the
  release's checksum file). Both versions were run against both repositories: 1.7.7 reports that
  one label and nothing else; 1.7.10 reports nothing. The macOS job itself had started on
  `macos-26`, so the label is real. A gate tool is run at the version CI pins.

`env["X"]`, `raw(env, "X")`, `resolveSetting("X")` and the environment contract's declarations —
and requires a row for each whose name says it is a secret (secret, password, private, token, a
key or key id, a DSN, a CA bundle) or that is a URL carrying a password (`DATABASE_URL`,
`DATABASE_OWNER_URL`, `VALKEY_URL`). Three names are excepted, each with why: `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_API_KEY`
and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` are read only to be refused or named at boot; `SENTRY_DSN` is not a
secret (Sentry, "Data Source Name (DSN)": "DSNs are safe to keep public because they only allow
submission of new events"). Self-tests on a scratch tree, every way of reading included. This
repository's register gains a row for each of the 21 deployment secrets the platform's code reads
— held by each app's deployment, never here (platform-foundation has none) — and `FIXTURE_SECRET`,
the name a unit test gives a made-up feature's setting, recorded as what it is.

**N-32 — an unknown expiry has a deadline.** `scripts/check-credential-expiry.mjs` passed "unknown"
with a warning, forever. An "unknown" row now needs `pending-owner-until` (a real date, today or
later, at most 90 days ahead) and `owner-step` (what the owner does to find the date): it warns,
naming the date and the step, until that day and fails the day after — in the weekly check and in
CI, where the register test fails on it — and fails at once without both.

**N-77 — the ACRCloud credit is watched.** ACRCloud is prepaid and offers no balance API: its
console API has projects, buckets and an undocumented daily statistic, and its identification
answers carry no quota header (docs.acrcloud.com, "Identification API", "Console API → Base
Projects", "Error Codes" — 3003 "Request count limit exceeded" is the only sign, at exhaustion).
So the platform counts what ACRCloud bills, as ACRCloud defines it — "Valid Requests = Requests with
results + Requests with no results / 2" (docs.acrcloud.com, FAQ "Definition of Terms") — after
each answered identification, in migration 069's `provider_usage` (platform-owned, in halves),
through `provider_usage_add` (one statement: no count lost across instances) and
`provider_usage_read`, the only access the request role has. `ACRCLOUD_CREDIT_ALERT_AT` is the
operator's budget in valid requests: the request that reaches it raises
`credentials.acrcloud_credit_low` once (log, metric, error report), and readiness's
`song-id-credit` (the song-id module's, degraded-only) is degraded from then on — and while
ACRCloud serves with no budget set. After a top-up the budget is raised (ROTATION_RUNBOOK,
"Credit"); the count is never edited by hand. An error answer is not counted; a count that cannot
be written never fails the identification.

at readiness (`agent-delegation-keys`) and at the token route (the coded 503, not a 500): its
entry has the detail. ENV_REFERENCE says what an app that runs both halves checks.

skipped on every run, unnoticed. The step now receives `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, and

reads, directly or through a constant, must reach every step that runs `npm run test:e2e` — in its
`env:`, its job's, or `$GITHUB_ENV` from an earlier step; self-tests for each form.

**NEW-2 and N-109 — the promotion guides.** Playform's guide said the record check shows
"twenty-three rows"; the files from `046` were 27 after 065–068, and are 28 with 069. Every count
in both guides was checked against the files: MIGRATION_v5_to_v6 said 067 locks "five tables" —
it adds columns to four (`config_pending_approvals`, `platform_config_history`, `review_queue`,
`content_safety_audit`); the rest hold (060's four settings, 064's eight keys, the replay's three

MIGRATION_v5_to_v6 copies every platform migration from 046 once; an app's guide
(`docs/<APP>_MIGRATION_v…_to_v….md`) has its record count, its §1 table and its pbcopy list equal
to the files from 046, and names the newest platform migration as the last a database applies. Both

(MIGRATION_v5_to_v6 step 5; Playform's "Order of work"), with the check after it.

**Tests.** `credential-register` (N-33 scan and self-test; N-32's rule and its CI self-test);
`acrcloud-credit` (the budget, the count, the alert once, the probe in each state, an
identification counted as billed — error answers not); `db/provider-usage.db` (concurrent requests
add up through the request role; the table itself refused); the replay's 069 step (grants,
totals, a malformed name and a negative count refused, applied twice changing nothing);
`e2e-key-wiring`; `migration-guide-counts`.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** the credential register test and both registers; the expiry script; the song-id
  module (its identifier, a new usage file, a probe); a new migration (069) with the replay's checks
  and the platform migration list; the retention and user-data registers (`provider_usage`: kept,
  no person's data — their DB coverage tests found it); PF's CI workflow (the E2E step and a key
  check); both promotion
  guides, ENV_REFERENCE, ROTATION_RUNBOOK; two new guards.
- **Races:** concurrent identifications on any number of instances each add in one statement
  (`insert … on conflict do update … returning`): none lost, the alert raised by the one request
  whose own total crossed the budget.
- **Dependencies down:** the database down → the count is logged and skipped, the identification
  stands, the probe is degraded ("could not be read"); ACRCloud down → nothing billed, nothing
  counted.
- **Erasure leftovers:** none: `provider_usage` holds a provider's name and a number, no person's
  data (platform-owned, no tenant).
- **Screens × responses:** no screen changes; readiness and /api/health list one more probe by name
  and status (details stay in the log).
- **Journeys touched:** none changed; e2e spec by spec on both repositories, base and change; in CI
  PF's model journey now runs instead of skipping.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No: the new table is reached only through two owner-rights
  functions that take a provider's name and a count, granted to the request role only; the public
  roles reach neither (replay checks both).

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** the request role's new access (069's two functions); the workflow's E2E step
  receiving the model and Google keys.
- **Actors that exist today:** any signed-in account (or guest, where song identification is
  offered) spends ACRCloud credit with each identification — bounded by `SONG_IDENTIFY_RULE` and
  the daily paid quota — and the readiness probe spends it too; this change makes that spending
  visible before it ends the service. Pull requests run CI: a Dependabot PR gets no secrets (the
  warning path); a pull request from a fork gets none either and fails the key check, as Playform's
  E2E layer already does. No actor gains a capability: the count is written only by server code.
- **Bypasses:** none new: `provider_usage_add` refuses a malformed provider name and a count
  outside 0–1000; the table itself is not granted to the request role.
- **Forgeries:** a client cannot add to or read the count — no route takes it; the functions run
  only from the identification path and the probe.
- **Legitimate flows:** an operator sets and raises the budget; an identification is counted; CI's
  E2E step runs the model journey with the key.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for sub-batch 55l (2026-11-10): N-68, N-33, N-32, N-77,
  the PF CI E2E key, the guide counts and N-109.

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** every reader of `getAcrCloudConfig` (the module, the identifier, the
  feature check — the new field is additive); every importer of the song-id module's probes
  (`createModuleHealthProbes`, the dependency-coverage test); the replay's platform-table and
  function lists; every workflow step that runs `test:e2e` in both repositories; every reader of
  the registers (the expiry script and the weekly workflow).
- **Hostile re-read:** a budget of `0`, `1.5` or `1e3` (refused: unset); a count crossing the budget
  from two instances at once (each total is the statement's own, so exactly one crosses); a
  register row "unknown" with a date 10 years ahead (refused past 90 days) or a rolled-over date
  (`2026-02-31`, refused); an E2E skip through a constant (`OWNER_URL`, read through); a key
  written to `$GITHUB_ENV` by a later step (not counted — tested by order).

**The assistant page.** `/assistant` (`app/assistant/AssistantClient.tsx`,
`components/assistant/AssistantPanel.tsx`), reached from the home page's bar ("Assistant", for a

**What the guard found besides, and what was done.** Three platform files only tests load — moved

**Tests (N-119).** `screening-refusal` (the mapping; `checkSafety`'s decision for a blocklist

`agent-approve`, `extract`, `identify`, `transcribe`, `profile-api` (a blocked field appealable,

**Tests.** `reachable-modules` (the guard; self-tests); `mounted-screens` (on the shared walk,
unchanged in what it checks); `assistant-page` (the page against the route's own answers: signed
out, loading, a guest, a question sent as the user and its answer, Ctrl+Enter, a cut-off answer,
rejected content with its decision's link, an answer withheld mid-stream with none, a rate limit, a
guest token refused, a lost connection and Try again, Stop and a later question untouched by the
stopped one, Clear, the bound; the home bar's link, none for a guest); route fixtures produced by
`/api/stream`'s handler (an answer, a cut-off answer, an answer withheld, rejected content, a
guest, a rate limit — the event stream recorded as sent); `stream-events` (unchanged, still on the

accessibility checks (axe, WCAG 2 AA): the assistant's failed on the base colour. **E2E** (`e2e/assistant.spec.ts`, the same file in
both repositories), as its own test-double user (`asker-q`, `platform/auth/mock-provider.ts`;

refusal (422) shown by its message → its decision on `/account`; an ordinary question → the screen
shows exactly what the route answered (with no model key, the route's refusal); with the model
(CI's key) the answer streams and completes; at 390 px nothing overflows. Its own user because the
blocked question records a decision against the account that asked: on the default e2e user it
restricted that account, and Playform's later profile and notification journeys were refused
(found by the first change run).

Walked at 1280 and 390 px on production builds of the base and the change.

**N-119: only a block is `content.rejected` (found by the walk).** With no model key the assistant
answered an ordinary question "This content does not meet our guidelines", with "See this decision
and appeal it". The walk's database showed why it was wrong: the screening had recorded nothing to
appeal — the classifier was unreachable, so the content was withheld unjudged (never queued, never
a decision). Every route answered `content.rejected` to any input `checkSafety` refused — a block
(a decision recorded against the account, which the account page lists and an appeal can reach),
an escalation (queued for a moderator; only a block can be appealed — `review-service`), and an
outage alike — and to the model's own output withheld (no decision about the user at all); and
every screen links `content.rejected` to the appeal (TASK-210). The owner's decision (2026-11-09):
a hold is its own code, with no appeal; the link stays only on a real block.

- **The screening's decision.** `checkSafety` (`lib/safety.ts`) carries `decision` — `block`,
  `escalate` or `unjudged` (`SafetyResult`, `types/index.ts`), from the pipeline's action and
  `screeningUnavailable`; `classifyContent` carries it on its result.
- **One answer for it:** `lib/screening-refusal.ts`, `screeningRefusal` — block →
  `content.rejected` (422, appealable); escalate → `content.held_for_review` (422, new: "This is
  waiting for a moderator to review it before it can be used. Nothing more is needed from you.");
  unjudged → `service.unavailable` (503, `service: moderation`: try again). No decision (a
  screening that predates it) is answered as held: never an appeal for a decision that may not
  exist. Pure, so code with injected effects uses it too.
- **Every input screening answers by it:** platform-foundation's `/api/process` and
  `/api/stream`; Playform's `/api/process`, `/api/stream`, `/api/tts`,
  `/api/agent/process-content` and the translate session (`lib/translate-session.ts`, through
  `/api/translate/dispatch`). Playform's profile route answers by each field's decision
  (`profileRefusal`, `platform/auth/profile-screening.ts`): a blocked field is named in
  `appealFields` (the only fields the page offers to appeal — a field refused for its length or
  shape, or warned, is not a decision); all held → `content.held_for_review`; all unjudged →
  `service.unavailable`.
- **Model output withheld is `content.withheld`** (422, new, no appeal): the stream's coded end,
  `/api/process`'s translations, and Playform's agent workflow and approved step, extract,
  identify, transcribe and the translate session's translations.
- **Screens.** `content.held_for_review` is its own refusal kind, `held`: a gray status (a wait,
  not a failure) with no appeal or retry (`RefusalNotice`; Playform's notifications at info level).
  `content.rejected` keeps the appeal link — now only ever a block.
- **The account page** does not list holds: an escalation's outcome is a review case the page does
  not read, so listing holds is not a small change; the hold's message promises nothing about the
  account page.
- **The guard:** `__tests__/screening-refusal.test.ts` — no production source names
  `content.rejected` but the mapping and the files that define and render the code; every source
  that calls `checkSafety` answers through `screeningRefusal` (or injects it into code that does,
  named in the guard). Self-tests on scratch sources and a scratch tree.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** the home page's bar (both repositories); a new page and component; the stream hook
  and its parser (no other caller); the shared refusal notice (read, unchanged); the catalog
  (`screens.assistant`, `screens.home.assistant`); the route-fixture producer; the journey
  register; the platform's file list (`platform-paths.json`).
- **Races:** a new question while one streams: the old one is aborted and its events dropped (the
  hook compares its own controller); Ask is replaced by Stop while streaming.
- **Dependencies down:** the model or the classifier down → the route's coded refusal
  (`service.unavailable` — for the screening, `moderation`, N-119 below), shown by its message,
  with Try again; the connection lost → the network refusal.
- **Erasure leftovers:** none: the page stores nothing; a blocked question's decision is recorded
  as every screening's is (already in the erasure register).
- **Screens × responses:** the page against fixtures the handler produced, for every answer kind
  the route sends.
- **Journeys touched:** home → assistant; a blocked question → account page; e2e spec by spec on
  both repositories, base and change.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No: the route, its guard, its limits and its screening are
  unchanged; the page only calls it as the signed-in user.

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** a signed-in account's question to the paid model through `/api/stream`.
- **Actors that exist today:** any signed-in account could already call `/api/stream` by hand
  (TASK-133's verified guard, `AI_PER_USER`, the daily paid quota, input and output screening —
  all unchanged); the page adds no capability, only the screen. Guests are refused by the route
  and shown no form. A child's account is held by the consent gate (`stream` is a gated feature),
  shown by its refusal.
- **Bypasses:** none new: the page sends only the question; the system prompt, tier and token
  bounds are the server's (`stream-policy`).
- **Disclosure:** the answer goes to the account that asked; a refusal shows the catalog's
  message, never the classifier's words.
- **Forgeries:** the page names no account and sends no id: the route takes the account from the
  verified token, so a crafted request asks as its own sender only; a journey exemption cannot be
  added to pass (the register only shrinks: `/api/stream` left it, none was added).
- **Legitimate flows:** a user asking a question and reading the answer; stopping it; appealing a
  blocked question from its link.
- **N-119:** the refusal's code is chosen by the server from the screening's own decision; no
  caller input selects it. A user learns their content was held rather than blocked — already
  true of the refusal itself (the content was not used), and it names no category, reason or
  reviewer. Nothing is opened: a hold or an outage still refuses the content, as before.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for sub-batch 55k (2026-11-09); N-119, the owner's decision of the same day (its own code for a hold, the appeal only on a block).

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** every importer of the stream hook (the new panel only) and of
  `consumeStreamEvents` (the hook, `stream-events.test.ts`); every reader of the three moved files
  (their tests, and comments naming them); the journey register; the risk tiers (Playform's

- **Hostile re-read:** a question at the bound (the textarea's `maxLength`; the route refuses past
  it anyway); a second question while one streams (the first aborted, its late events dropped —
  tested); a guest (no form, nothing sent); a refusal mid-answer (no appeal link — tested); the
  guard's own entry rules (a comment or a data file naming a path is not an entry — tested).
- **Found in the batch and fixed in it:** N-119 (above) — every refusal of screened input, and
  of withheld model output, offered an appeal for a decision that did not exist unless the input
  was blocked; white text on `bg-blue-600` is 3.76:1, under WCAG 2 AA's
  4.5:1 — found by the assistant journey's accessibility check on its Ask button; the same pair was

  the account page, the review dashboard, the admin console's panels, the refusal notice's retry, the

  the journey's blocked question restricting the shared e2e user (its own identity now);

  three test-only modules in `platform/`; the README's hook list (a profile hook and the channel
