### TASK-210 — Residuals 55j: the moderator's review queue and the member's appeal on real pages, and no screen component left on no page

| Field        | Detail                                                                                          |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**       | TASK-210                                                                                        |
| **Type**     | Defect (a moderation flow no one could use: the review queue and the appeal mounted on no page) |
| **Severity** | Medium (N-117)                                                                                  |
| **Phase**    | Phase 5                                                                                         |
| **Target**   | v6.0.0 (RC)                                                                                     |
| **Status**   | Fixed on develop (sub-batch 55j of the residuals batch)                                         |
| **Logged**   | 2026-11-09 (register N-117, found by sub-batch 55i)                                             |

Sub-batch 55j of the residuals register, in both repositories (Playform: its TASK-5011).

**What was found (N-117).** The review dashboard (`components/ReviewDashboard`) and the appeal
form (`components/AppealForm`) were imported by no page of either repository. Traced end to end:

- **A moderator** (the `moderator` role: `can_access_admin`, `can_moderate`, `admin_view_audit`,
  migration 018) signs in to `/admin` and is offered Approvals, Audit log, Capabilities and
  Tenant (`AdminShell`'s mapping): no section reads `/api/moderation/review`. The queue's routes
  (`GET`/`POST /api/moderation/review`, `PATCH /api/moderation/review/[id]`, `POST …/assist`,
  `PATCH /api/moderation/appeals/[id]`) were reachable only by hand-made requests; the journey
  register exempted all five ("pending the staff journeys").
- **A member** whose text the Guardian blocks sees `content.rejected` on the home page ("message":
  no action), or `account.restricted` after strikes (sign-out only — though the registry's action
  for it reads "Show the restriction; offer appeal"). No screen shows them a decision's id, and
  `POST /api/moderation/appeals` requires one: no one using the product could appeal.
- There was no account page (`/account`), no moderation page, and no duplicate path: the
  components were the only screens for these routes. So they are mounted, not removed.

**The moderator's path.** The admin console's **Moderation** section (`AdminShell`, permission
`can_moderate`, the one every moderation route checks; `app/admin/page.tsx` renders the review
dashboard there, with no command bar — the queue is decided item by item). On the dashboard: an
appeal is claimed, released and resolved through its own route (`/api/moderation/appeals/[id]`,
which refuses any other item), every other item through the review route; a refused action shows
the refusal's own message (`readRefusal`; it showed the body's compatibility field); the item's
source, priority, status, trigger, action and the assistant's suggested decision are the catalog's
words (`screens.review_dashboard.*`; a code a newer server sends reads as itself); each resolve
control is named by its label (`useId`); and a reason recorded before the keys, whose disclosure
is a `<details>`, is no longer inside a `<p>` (invalid HTML: React warned of a hydration error).

**The member's path.** `GET /api/moderation/appeals` (new): the caller's own blocks of their own
input (`listOwnDecisions`, `platform/moderation/review-service.ts`), newest first, each with its
appeal if one was filed, and the rules an appeal is held to (window, reason length). The account
is the verified token's (no parameter is read); a restricted, suspended or banned account still
reads it (the decision under appeal is often why). `/account` (new page,
`app/account/AccountClient.tsx`): the decisions about their content
(`components/account/ModerationDecisions.tsx`) — what was blocked and when, until when it can be
appealed, the appeal form under it (with the server's limits; its field's id unique on the page),
a sent appeal confirmed and the list read again, the appeal's standing (waiting, in review,
decided: stands, overturned or changed), or the window closed. It is reached from the home page's
bar ("Your account", signed-in users) and from where a decision is seen: the refusal of rejected
content or of a restricted account links to it (`RefusalNotice`'s `AppealLink`, `offersAppeal`;
platform-foundation's demo home, Playform's notifications) — never for a guest, who has no account.
The appeal form's confirmation no longer promises a notification the platform does not send.

**Found by the journey: no decision recorded its account.** The e2e journey's member was blocked
and the account page listed nothing: the Guardian built its audit record from the result alone
(`platform/moderation/audit.ts`) and never passed the screening context's user id, so
`content_safety_audit.user_id` was null on every decision. So the appeals route's ownership check
(the decision's account must be the appellant's) refused every appeal even when sent by hand, no
account could find its decisions, and an account's data export and erasure (by `user_id`) never
reached them. Now the Guardian records the account (`logModerationAudit(…, context.userId)`), and
**migration 068** gives the rows written before theirs where a strike the Sentinel gave for the
decision, or an escalation or ban review of it, names one account that exists and is not erased (an
ambiguous one, an erased account's, or a decision nothing names stays without one). The replay
applies 068 again over such rows and reads them back; the verification query is in
MIGRATION_v5_to_v6 (TASK-210).

**The guard.** `__tests__/mounted-screens.test.ts`: every source file under `components/` is
reached from a file under `app/` by imports (static, `import()`, `require`), transitively — a
component only an unmounted one imports is unmounted too; a test is never a path. Its known list
is per repository, minimal and justified in the guard: platform-foundation's
`components/AdaptiveInput/` (the platform's input component, shipped for a consumer's screen —
Playform's home mounts it; the platform's demo home has no conductor), Playform's empty. A known
entry that is reached or names nothing fails. Self-tests on a scratch app.

**What the guard found besides, and what was done.**

- **The profile screen** (`components/auth/ProfilePage.tsx`, `VisibilitySelect.tsx`,
  `hooks/useProfileForm.ts`): on no page in either repository. The platform has no profile route;
  Playform has (`GET`/`PUT /api/profile`, screened). The screen went with its route: removed here
  (with its test and its catalog entries, `screens.auth.profile`, `screens.auth.visibility`), and
  Playform's own from this commit, mounted at its `/profile` (its TASK-5011). The shared
  `effect-free-state` test's profile-form case moved with it.
- **Playform's Teams panel and its cards** — Playform's own (its TASK-5011).

**Tests.** `mounted-screens` (the guard, self-tests); `moderation-guardian` and `moderation-audit`
(a decision recorded against its account, none for a guest); the replay's 068 step (six rows: a
strike's, an escalation's, an erased account's, two accounts', none, one already set); `own-decisions` (the service on the real
in-memory stores: own rows only, however a store spells an id; the appeal read past its limit;
the window); `moderation-appeals-routes` (GET: the caller's own whatever the query names, no
session or no account, a restricted account, the store down, the id as stored); route fixtures
from the handlers (`GET /api/moderation/appeals` — none, appealable, past its window, waiting, in
review, upheld, the store failing; a pending appeal in the queue; an appeal claimed);
`moderation-decisions`, `account-page` (the page, the home bar's link), `review-dashboard` (the
appeal's route, the catalog's words, labelled controls, an unknown code), `admin-console-first-section`
(a moderator's sections, the Moderation section read and shown), `refusal-handler` (which
refusals offer the appeal), `appeal-form` (two forms on a page, the confirmation),
`component` (the demo home's rejection links to its appeal; a guest's does not),
`mock-provider-admins` (the journey's moderator and member), the role matrix (the new method).
**E2E** (`e2e/moderation.spec.ts`, the same file in both repositories): a member's blocked text →
the refusal's link → `/account` → appeal; the moderator's console → Moderation → the assistant
(no suggestion without a model) → claim → overturn; an escalation filed through the route
claimed and released; the member sees the appeal decided and is refused the queue. The five
moderation exemptions are gone from `journey-exemptions.json` (32 → 27); none added.
`e2e/baseline.spec.ts` (platform-foundation's): on a phone the demo home's buttons stay inside
their card.

Walked at 1280 and 390 px on production builds of the base and the change: the member's home,
the home after a blocked text, `/account` (decisions, an appeal open), the moderator's console and
its Moderation section (pending and resolved). The moderator's journey waits out the console's shared rate limit
(admin:ops, 30 a minute per address) that the admin specs before it spend.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** the admin console's navigation and page; the review dashboard and the appeal form;
  the appeals route (a new method) and the review service; the home page's bar; the shared
  refusal notice (every screen that shows one: the admin console's panels and command bar too —
  a restricted administrator is offered their decisions as anyone is); the platform's demo home
  and its seam; the catalog; the test double's identities; the journey register; the platform's
  file list (`platform-paths.json`: the profile screen is no longer the platform's).
- **Races:** none new: the list is a read; an appeal is filed by the existing route (one per
  decision, refused when pending — unchanged); 068 updates only rows with no account, in one
  statement.
- **Dependencies down:** the list's stores unreadable → `503 service.unavailable` (moderation),
  shown by its message with a retry; the assistant down → no suggestion (fail-open, unchanged).
- **Erasure leftovers:** none new: the list reads `content_safety_audit` and `review_queue`,
  already in the register — and with the account now recorded (and 068's backfill), an account's
  decisions are exported and detached on erasure as the register says (they were not reached
  before). 068 never attaches a decision to an erased account.
- **Screens × responses:** the account page and the dashboard against the routes' own answers
  (fixtures produced by the handlers).
- **Journeys touched:** the member's home → account → appeal; the moderator's console →
  Moderation; e2e spec by spec on both repositories, base and change.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No: the list runs in the caller's tenant (`tenantRoute`), on
  the caller's own rows.

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** a signed-in account reading the decisions about its own content; a moderator's
  console offering the queue.
- **Actors that exist today:** members whose content is blocked (any signed-in account: the route
  takes the account from the verified token and reads no parameter — a query naming another
  account is ignored, tested); guests (refused: no account; no link is shown to them);
  moderators and administrators (the section shows only with `can_moderate`; every route checks
  it — the section is display only).
- **Bypasses:** none: the console's section mapping is display only, as every section's; the
  list reads only rows whose account is the caller's (`sameId` after the store's own filter).
- **Disclosure:** a decision's id, time, content type and appeal standing go to the account they
  are about — already in that account's data export. The decision's reasons, the classifier's
  words and the reviewer's notes are not sent.
- **Forgeries:** no caller names the account a decision is recorded against: the code records
  the account the verified request ran as (the screening context's, set by the route from its guard); 068 attributes a past
  decision only from the platform's own records of it — a strike, a review case — never from
  input, and leaves one two records disagree on.
- **Legitimate flows:** a member appealing a block, including a restricted or banned account (the
  list is not gated on standing); a moderator deciding an appeal.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for sub-batch 55j (2026-11-09).

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** every importer of `RefusalNotice` (the admin console, its panels and
  command bar, the users panel) — the link appears only for a moderation decision; every reader of
  `AppealForm`'s props; `permittedSections` (the console's first section and every test of it);
  the journey register; the role matrix; the route fixtures.
- **Hostile re-read:** a query naming another account (ignored); an appeal of another account's
  decision (refused by the existing ownership check, unchanged); an appeal on the escalation's
  route (`/review/[id]` accepts it as before; the dashboard uses the appeal's own); a code the
  catalog lacks (shown as itself); a decision past its window (no form); two forms on the page
  (ids unique); a guest (no link, no page content read).
- **Found in the batch and fixed in it:** every moderation decision recorded without its account
  (so no appeal could pass, and no account's export or erasure reached them) — the code and
  migration 068; the dashboard's PATCH error read the body's alias; its
  codes shown raw; its resolve controls unlabelled; a `<details>` inside a `<p>`; the appeal form's
  fixed field id and its promise of a notification; `account.restricted`'s "offer appeal" never
  offered; the demo home's three buttons ran past their card at 390 px (they wrap now — found
  by the walk). Nothing found is left.

### TASK-209 — Residuals 55i: the platform's notes written by code in the catalog, settings and permissions named by the catalog, a deterministic erasure test

| Field        | Detail                                                                                               |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**       | TASK-209                                                                                             |
| **Type**     | Defect (English TypeScript stored and every reader saw; definitional English on screens; flaky test) |
| **Severity** | Low (N-112, N-113, N-114)                                                                            |
| **Phase**    | Phase 5                                                                                              |
| **Target**   | v6.0.0 (RC)                                                                                          |
| **Status**   | Fixed on develop (sub-batch 55i of the residuals batch)                                              |
| **Logged**   | 2026-11-09 (register N-112, N-113, N-114, found by sub-batch 55h)                                    |

Sub-batch 55i of the residuals register, in both repositories (Playform: its TASK-5010).

**N-112 — the platform's notes TypeScript wrote are a catalog key and values (or a code).**
TASK-208 moved the notes SQL wrote; the platform's TypeScript still composed English into the
same records. Now each is kept as the catalog's key and values (`platform/errors/recorded-text.ts`,
`screens.records.*`, `screens.held.note_*`) or a code, and rendered where it is read; what a
person wrote stays theirs, as written:

- **A held change's decision** (`proposals`): a lapsed hold's and an undecided one's note
  (`expiredUnused`, `expiredUndecided`); the decision routes' default notes when a person wrote
  none (`rejected_after_run_failed`, "verified that its run did not take effect", "verified as
  applied", "approved again: …"); a refused or stale hold's why; a superseded hold's
  (hold-withdrawal: a power reduction, every agent suspended — the operator's reason a value);
  the action pipeline's revised and stale-state notes; a duplicate hold's. The stores take a
  `DecisionNote` (`platform/kernel/types.ts`): a person's string goes to `decision_note`, the
  platform's key and values to `decision_shown` — inside a withdrawal's record as its `note`.
  "Marked executed by …", written into `last_run_error`, is the record
  `screens.records.marked_executed` (who, and their note); the run's note is cleared and the
  approval's decider stands.
- **A kept run's note** (`last_run_error`) is a code: the run's own (`approvals.run_failed`…) or
  a `screens.held.note_*` key (run failed, commit failed, state moved, the two lease notes, which
  were English matched back on screen). `runNoteShown` words it for the Approvals screen and the
  export; a held trajectory's step carries it as `lastRunError`, beside the decider's `note` and
  the platform's `decision`.
- **A two-person approval** (`config_pending_approvals`): the system's withdrawal (stale,
  refused, a required job) and a supersession are `review_shown` (new); a request's comment the
  platform made is `change_shown` (new); the impact summary (English derived from the row's key
  and values, shown nowhere) is no longer written.
- **A setting's change** (`platform_config_history.change_shown`, new): "Changed on the config
  page", "Use the platform default", "Set by an operator for this tenant", "Approved: <the
  request's comment>", an emergency suspension's, the command bar's summary — the last rendered
  in English when written. The screens no longer send their own catalog words as a comment (the
  tenant settings and dual-control panels did). The config tools take the note as `changeShown`,
  a key the server sets (`CONFIG_SERVER_SET_INPUTS`; a caller's is refused).
- **The Sentinel**: a ban's reason is `users.ban_note` (TASK-208's column), a strike's reason a
  code (`guardian_block:<what triggered it>`, worded with the row's category and severity on
  export). **The escalation reaper's** note is `review_queue.notes_shown` (new). **The effect
  ledger's** reasons are catalog keys. **job_claim**'s dead lease (050, SQL) records the code
  `lease_expired`, worded by the Jobs console, as the in-memory store does.
- **Rows written before are migrated** by migration 067 (`067_recorded_notes_written_by_code.sql`),
  matched exactly — a person's text inside a composed one ("Approved: …", an operator's reason)
  kept as a value, anything else left as it is; 062's `review_comment` too. Replayed in
  `migration-replay.sh` with rows as the code before wrote them, applied twice; 050 applied again
  is followed by 067 (it redefines 050's job_claim). MIGRATION_v5_to_v6 has the procedure and a
  verification query (every count 0).
- **The guard — rule F of `screen-text-indirect`:** no TypeScript in app/api, platform/, lib/ or
  the screens writes words into a record's note, reason, comment or error — an object's stored
  field, a statement's parameter into a note or code column, or an argument a function stores
  (followed through its parameters to a fixed point); a catalog render reaching one is reported
  too (its words would be stored in one locale). With a `[self-test]`; its known list is empty.
  On the base it reports 105 sites (the batch's additions included).

**N-113 — a setting's description and a permission's name are the catalog's.** Migrations write
them in English (`platform_config.description`, `permissions.display_name`, `description`), and
the config page, the operator's tenant settings, the tenant settings panel, the Roles page and
the admin search showed that English. Now each is the catalog's, by key and code
(`platform/errors/definitions.ts`: `screens.settings.<key>`,
`screens.permissions.<code>.name|description`; an app's own under `screens.app.…`): the config
answers carry the description as a key the screens render, the Roles page's names are the
catalog's in the request's language and ordered by them (the search's permission rows too: the
statement is given the catalog's names by code), a search's cells are keys. **Decision (ADR-051, D4's
implementation note):** the stored English stays as the definitional record — the configuration
assistant (the model) reads it and the admin search matches it — and no screen or answer a screen
shows reads it. **The guard** (`scripts/catalog-definitions-check.mjs`, run by
`scripts/migration-replay.sh` on its database before any test writes to it;
`__tests__/catalog-definitions-guard.test.ts` holds the replay to it and plants each gap): every
setting and permission the migrations define has its entries in every locale the catalog has
(English today, ADR-051 D6), and the catalog names none the database lacks. First written as a
DB test reading the shared test database, it saw another suite's setting in one of ten parallel
runs (the N-114 proof): the replay's database holds only what the migrations define.

**Added in the batch (the coordinator's scope correction) — the same class, to zero:**

- **An audit record's details** carry no English TypeScript composed. A run's failure reason,
  audited as `approved_run_failed`, `approved_run_indeterminate` and `action_applied_not_recorded`
  (`platform/agents/tool-invoker.ts`), was English carried by the error (`RUN_RAISED`, the two
  completion reasons in the action pipeline); each is now a catalog key
  (`screens.records.run_raised`, `completion_not_written`, `claim_taken_back`). The audit log page
  (`GET /api/admin/audit`) and the data export render the platform's words in the details — a
  record (`changeShown`) or a records key — in the reader's language
  (`platform/errors/recorded-words.ts` `renderRecordedDeep`); codes, ids and a person's text stay
  as they are. Raw text from a provider, a model or an error goes only under a key named `raw…`,
  which nothing shows (none today: R-77 keeps an error's text in the log). **Rule F** now also
  sinks every value of an audit record's details (the `details` of an object naming its
  `action`) and follows a sink that reads an error's field (`err.reason`) to each `new` of the
  class it is known to be (a parameter typed as it, an `instanceof`, a `new`); with a self-test.
- **The Sentinel's reasoning** (`SentinelResult.reasoning`) is a list of catalog keys and values
  (`screens.sentinel.*`), one per line, not English joined by the agent.
- **The configuration assistant's change preview** (`ConfigChangeRequest.impact`,
  `affectedUsers`, in the config tools' answers) is composed from the catalog
  (`screens.config_impact.*`): the change, then what its tier, kind or key touches; who it
  affects.
- **Three suites Jest reported "focused", not "passed"** (risk-tier, roadmap-consistency,
  review-process): no `.only` — Jest's status for a file where every test ran passed but not every
  test ran. Thirteen tests were skipped by a condition on the repository they ran in
  (`(has ? it : it.skip)`): in the platform, a consuming app's checks never ran, and the gates'
  totals counted them as "skipped". Each now runs in both repositories and says what holds in the
  other; the proposal-store contract's two arms skipped without a fixture take it as required;
  data-layer uses the shared database gate. **The guard** (`__tests__/no-skipped-tests.test.ts`):
  no test file or helper focuses, skips, leaves to do or expects to fail a test (`.only`, `.skip`,
  `.todo`, `.failing`, `fit`, `xit`, `xdescribe`…, in code, not in strings), the two availability
  gates aside (`dbDescribe`, `valkeyDescribe`), each checked to fail under its `REQUIRE_…`
  variable as CI runs; with self-tests. A consumer's proposal-store fixture must now give
  `markUndecided` and `trajectoryWithCommitment`.
- **The moderation pipeline's reasons** (the coordinator's second correction): the Guardian's
  reasoning and context factors, a rating level's name (`config.ts`), the classifier's own notes,
  the modality, input-screen, image-generation and RAG screens' reasons, a RAG explanation's
  steps and conclusion, and the profile and social refusals were English composed in TypeScript
  — stored in `content_safety_audit` and a review case's `moderation_result`, shown to moderators
  on the review dashboard and returned in an appeal's answer. Each is a catalog key and values
  (`platform/moderation/reasons.ts`, `screens.moderation.*`); the catalog carries the words they
  had, so a moderator and a user read the same text (`__tests__/moderation-reasons.test.tsx`
  compares every template's rendering with the English expression it replaced, value for value).
  `content_safety_audit` gains `reasoning_shown` and `context_factors_shown` (checked arrays of
  keys); 067 converts the rows written before — the reasoning part by part (all of it or none),
  each factor, the classifier's notes — and a text that is not a template exactly keeps its
  stored text, which the dashboard shows as "a reason recorded before reasons were coded" with
  the stored text behind "Show the stored text" (N-108's pattern). The classifier model's own
  words are `rawReason` (raw model output, kept for the record, never shown as a screen's text);
  the platform's notes on its answer are `note`. **The prompt boundary:** the review
  assistant's prompt is model input, not a screen — the reasons are rendered there in English,
  the prompt's language, the same words it always carried (`review-assist.ts` PROMPT_LOCALE; a
  test pins the line). The review route's input check takes reasons and factors as keys the
  catalog has (a closed schema of their values). Rule F now sinks `reasoning`, `contextFactors`,
  `factors` and `conclusion`, a field assigned as well as one in an object literal; with a
  self-test. Neither the review dashboard nor the appeal form is mounted on a page in either
  repository (they are components for an app to mount); the walk mounts them on a scratch page.
  The data export does not carry the reasoning (its content_safety_audit section is the
  decision's codes); the new columns are classified in the register.
- **Locales:** English is the only locale the catalog defines (ADR-051 D6), and that is the
  owner's decision; the N-113 guard checks every locale `CATALOGS` defines, so a second one is
  held to the same entries the day it is added.

**N-114 — the erasure coverage test was intermittent; now deterministic.** Root cause: the
other account has two review cases (one the erased user decided, `r2`; one that mentions them,
`r3`), and the check read `where target_user_id = $1` with no order and took the first row. The
erasure's updates write new row versions wherever a page has room — which other sessions' writes
in the same database change — so `r3` ("pending") was sometimes first. Reproduced on the base
(four copies of the suite at once: the dump shows both rows); the read is now ordered and asserts
both. **The same class, found by running every DB suite in parallel nine times:**
`eligible-approvers` failed five times — "one super_admin alone" ran in a shared deployment,
where every tenant's operators may approve (`asOperator`), and suites beside it make operators of
their own; it now asks in a single-tenant deployment, as its premise says (the shared case is
proved beside it with an operator it made). Proved by ten consecutive runs of the affected shard
and of every DB suite in parallel, and the full gates.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** the proposal stores (both) and their contract kit; the approval routes and the
  operator's; the expiry job and run recovery; hold withdrawal; the action pipeline; the config
  stores, tools, governed writes, HTTP handlers, the kill switch and the command bar's agents and
  mappings; the review store and reaper; the Sentinel; the effect ledger; the job runner and
  job_claim; the data export; the Approvals, config, tenancy, dual-control, Roles and search
  screens; the erasure register (new columns classified); the moderation pipeline (the Guardian, its context, levels and classifier notes, the modality, input-screen, image and RAG screens, a RAG explanation), the review route and dashboard, the appeals answer, profile and social screening; the audit log page and the export's audit details.
- **Races:** none new: each record is written in the statement that decides, withdraws, bans or
  reaps; the marked-executed record by the same compare-and-set update.
- **Dependencies down:** a record whose key the catalog lacks cannot be stored (each new column's
  check takes only a `screens.` key; tests pin every key to English); a setting or permission
  without its entry fails the guard.
- **Erasure leftovers:** `review_shown` (who had approved: an administrative act, as
  `reviewed_by`), `change_shown` (a change's note), `notes_shown` (deleted with the case) are
  classified; `decision_shown`'s ids are replaced as before (`proposalsAbout`).
- **Screens × responses:** the config, tenant settings and operator settings answers (fixtures
  from the routes), the Roles answer, a search's cells; walked at 1280 and 390 px.
- **Journeys touched:** the admin console's config, Roles, search, Approvals and Audit log; the moderator's review dashboard and an appeal (scratch-mounted for the walk); Operator →
  Tenants → Settings; the e2e suites, spec by spec.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No: nothing new is read across tenants; the catalog is the
  platform's.

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** what the platform writes into a record and what screens and exports show of it.
- **Actors that exist today:** administrators and operators deciding and changing things, the
  configuration assistant (a model, through the config tools), the platform's jobs, a signed-in
  user exporting their data. The only new input is `changeShown` on the config tools: a caller's
  is refused (`request.field_not_accepted`), so only the platform's own code sets it.
- **Bypasses:** a new English note (rule F, at 0), a setting or permission without its entry
  (the DB guard).
- **Forgeries:** a person's note that looks like a key stays text (only the `_shown` columns are
  rendered as records); a note a person wrote that reads like the old English is migrated only on
  an exact match of the whole composed form.
- **Legitimate flows:** deciding, withdrawing, expiring and superseding holds; changing and
  resetting settings; the kill switch; banning; reaping; exporting.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for sub-batch 55i (2026-11-09).

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** every reader of `decisionNote`, `decisionShown`, `lastRunError`,
  `reviewComment`, `changeComment`, `reviewerNotes`, `banReason`, a strike's `reason`, the effect
  ledger's `error`, a job's `lastError`, a setting's `description` and a permission's name; both
  proposal stores; the contract kits; the erasure register.
- **Hostile re-read:** a person's note beginning like a platform note (left), a note on two lines
  (migrated whole), "Approved: " around the platform's own default (nested record), a command bar
  summary that does not read back exactly (left), a strike whose text names another category
  (left), an unknown run code (shown as recorded), a setting key the catalog lacks (no
  description shown; the guard fails), an app's own settings (its catalog).
- **Found in the batch and fixed in it (the coordinator's scope corrections, 2026-11-09):** the
  audit records' run-failure reasons, the Sentinel's reasoning lines, the configuration
  assistant's impact and affected users, three suites Jest reported "focused", and the
  moderation pipeline's reasons and their relatives (above). Nothing found is left.
- **The sweep before the gates** (the coordinator's rule 6): the recorded answers of every route
  (`__tests__/fixtures/route-responses*.json`) were read for English sentences, and every string
  literal of three words or more in a result field under platform/, lib/ and app/api was read
  for where it goes. What remains is one of: a person's own words (a comment, an appeal, a
  reviewer's notes); a catalog message rendered by the route in the reader's language (an
  error's `message`); text for a model or an agent — the config tools' descriptions and answers,
  a workflow's next-action descriptions (ADR-030: the agent's affordances), the review
  assistant's prompt — or the review assistant's `rationale` (the model's own suggestion, shown
  to a moderator as the model's); or a result's `error` or `reason` that only a log reads (coded
  results answer by their code, R-77). None is English the platform composes into a record or a
  screen.

### TASK-208 — Residuals 55h: the platform's notes on a record in the catalog, a held change's label that reads right

| Field        | Detail                                                                                   |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**       | TASK-208                                                                                 |
| **Type**     | Defect (English the database stored and every reader saw; labels composed into nonsense) |
| **Severity** | Low (N-110); N-111 Nit; one real screen defect found by the sweep (Low)                  |
| **Phase**    | Phase 5                                                                                  |
| **Target**   | v6.0.0 (RC)                                                                              |
| **Status**   | Fixed on develop (sub-batch 55h of the residuals batch)                                  |
| **Logged**   | 2026-11-09 (register N-110, N-111, found by sub-batch 55g)                               |

Sub-batch 55h of the residuals register, in both repositories (Playform: its TASK-5009).

**N-110 — the platform's notes on a record are a catalog key and values.** Ten statements in
platform/ wrote English into rows, on rule C's known list since TASK-207: a withdrawn approval's
decision note (`'Approved by ' || … || ', never run; withdrawn: ' || $3`, in `hold-expiry.ts` and
three statements of `postgres-proposal-store.ts`, one in its undecided form), an abandoned run's
reason (`postgres-trajectory-store.ts`), the note left where an erased one was (`user-data.ts`),
a carried-over ban's reason (`user-provisioning.ts`) and who acted in a subject's audit export
(`audit.ts`: "the platform", "another account"). Every reader saw them in English. Now:

- **The record is the catalog's key and values** (`platform/errors/recorded-text.ts`; its words,
  `recorded-words.ts`; `screens.records.*`): `proposals.decision_shown` keeps a withdrawal's record
  (who had approved it and when — the catalog's "unknown" when not recorded), and `decision_note`
  only the note given (why); `users.ban_note` keeps a carried-over ban's note, and `ban_reason` only
  what a person wrote; a run's step keeps its reason, an erased note's placeholder and a held
  decision's record (`decision`, beside its `note`) as keys; the audit export's `by` is a code
  (`platform`, `another_account`). The in-memory stores do the same (their English mirrors,
  `withdrawalNote` and `undecidedWithdrawalNote`, are gone). The SQL builds the objects inline with
  `jsonb_build_object` from the same keys (a test reads them from the statements).
- **Rendered where it is shown:** the subject's data export (`exportUserData`, the only place
  these reach a person) renders each from the catalog in the requester's language (the route
  negotiates it from `Accept-Language`); a person's own note is left as written
  (`renderRecords`).
- **Rows written before are migrated** by migration 066 (`066_recorded_notes.sql`), matched
  exactly — a note a person wrote is left as it is; 046's two English decision notes too —
  replayed twice in `migration-replay.sh` with rows as the code before wrote them, and
  documented in MIGRATION_v5_to_v6 with a verification query. No stored text is the only record
  of anything: each migrated note is rebuilt from its key and values word for word.
- **Rule C's known list is empty:** `screen-text-indirect` fails on any SQL string literal in
  app/api, platform/ or lib/ that holds words for a person.

**N-111 — a held erasure's label.** The one line for a held erasure was
`"Erase the account {account}"`, given "an account that is no longer found" (or "an account with
no address") when the account had no address to show: "Erase the account an account that is no
longer found". The template now selects on whether an address is given (`known`), so every
locale writes the whole sentence for each case.

**The sweep** — a label template given a sentence instead of a noun, and the reverse:

- A held change's line (`describeWhat`: "Erase the account …", "Setting …") was put inside
  sentences: "Mark {label} executed", "Approve {label} again", "Withdraw {label}: …",
  "Approve the held change {label}", "{key} is held for approval.", "Approve held change
  {what}", "{label} failed: …" (the jobs screen's action labels are imperatives too). Each now
  holds the label where a label stands ("Mark executed: {label} — …", "Approve the held change:
  {label}", "{label}: failed — {reason}"). Six `screens.held.result_*` messages built that way
  were used nowhere: removed.
- **Found and fixed — the tenant settings panel said "done" when a decision waits for a second
  approval.** It read the decision's answer as `pending`, which the route never sends (it answers
  `pendingApproval`), so an approval that now waits for a second one read "…: done.". It says
  what the Approvals panel says now ("Approved: … It now waits for a second approval"); the
  route's answer is a fixture its handler produced (`route-fixtures.test.ts`), and the test fails
  without the fix.
- **The guard — rule E of `screen-text-indirect`:** a held change's or an action's line
  (`describeWhat`, `describeAction`) is given to a catalog call only as its `label` or `what`, and
  every `{label}` and `{what}` in both catalogs stands where a label stands (at the start or after
  ": ", followed by the end, ":", ".", ",", " —" or a closing quote); with a `[self-test]`. On the
  base it reports the tenant panel's `{ key: describeWhat(h) }` and thirteen messages.
- Every account-naming line (`describeWhat`, `describeAction`) is rendered for each account a
  hold can name — an address, none, not found — and checked for a doubled noun phrase or a
  capital mid-line.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** the proposal stores (withdraw, supersede, an undecided run withdrawn), the approval
  expiry job, the trajectory-retention reaper, provisioning and the address sync (a carried ban),
  the strike ban and the unban (they clear the note), the soft delete and the erasure register,
  the data export and its route; the Approvals and tenant settings panels, the Jobs screen and
  the command bar's confirm step (wording). No route's answer changes but the export's words.
- **Races:** none new. Each record is written in the statement that decides, bans or reaps, from
  the row as it was (`decided_by`, `decided_at` read by the same `update`).
- **Dependencies down:** as before; a record whose key the catalog lacks cannot be stored (each
  column's check takes only a `screens.` key; a test pins every key the records use to English).
- **Erasure leftovers:** `decision_shown` is in the erasure's columns and statements (an id in it
  is replaced; a decision about the account loses its note, its record keeping the catalog's
  "erased" note); `ban_note` is cleared by the soft delete (`SOFT_DELETE_CLEARED`) and listed in
  the register. Tested (`user-data-coverage`, `approver-rules`).
- **Screens × responses:** the export (rendered, tested end to end on Postgres); the tenant
  settings panel's decision answer (fixture from the handler); labels walked at 1280 and 390 px.
- **Journeys touched:** the admin console's Approvals and Operator → Tenants → Settings (walked,
  base and change); the e2e suites, spec by spec.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No. The catalog is the platform's; nothing new is read
  across tenants; the export holds what it held, in the requester's words.

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** what the platform writes into a record, and what a data subject's export and an
  administrator's screen show of it.
- **Actors that exist today:** a signed-in user exporting their data; administrators and
  operators deciding held changes; the platform's jobs. None can do more with this change: every
  record is written by server code from fixed keys (`jsonb_build_object`), with values the row
  already held (an approver's id, a time); no route takes one from input; each column's check
  refuses any other shape.
- **Bypasses:** a new statement writing English (rule C, at 0); a label composed into a sentence
  (rule E).
- **Forgeries:** a person's note that looks like a key is text, not a record: only `decision_shown`
  and `ban_note` are rendered as records, and a note is a value inside one. A note a person wrote
  that happens to read like the old English is migrated only on an exact match of the whole
  composed form.
- **Legitimate flows:** deciding, withdrawing and expiring holds; the reaper; a ban following an
  address; exporting one's data; erasing an account.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for sub-batch 55h (2026-11-09).

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** every reader of `decisionNote` (the held trajectory's step,
  `gating.ts`), of `ban_reason` (the export's profile, the moderation types), of a step's `reason`
  and `note` (the export; no screen shows a step), of the audit export's rows; both proposal
  stores and the contract kit; the erasure register and its reconciliation tests.
- **Hostile re-read:** a decided-by that was null ('unknown', migrated to the catalog's word), a
  note on two lines (migrated whole), a person's note beginning "Approved by" (left), a step note
  already migrated (not read again: the second application changes nothing), an export row whose
  `by` is no code (left as it was), a record with an `errors.` key (not rendered as a record).
- **Found and left (reported to the register):** English the platform's TypeScript writes as a
  note (not SQL, so rule C does not see it): a lapsed hold's "expired: not run within N days of
  its approval" and an undecided one's, the decision routes' default notes ("verified that its
  run did not take effect", "rejected_after_run_failed"…), the action pipeline's superseded
  notes, a duplicate hold's note, "marked executed by …" in `last_run_error`, the strike ban's
  "Automatic ban: strike threshold exceeded", and 062's `review_comment`.

Sub-batch 55g of the residuals register, in both repositories (Playform: its TASK-5008).

**N-17 — every screen test's fetch answer is its route's.** `fake-fetch-baseline.json` excepted
196 hand-written bodies in 19 files here (Playform 253 in 24). Each is replaced by a fixture the
real route handler produced (`__tests__/route-fixtures.test.ts`, extended: the admin console's
session, Users and erasure, the kill switch, appeals, session renewal, MFA, Jobs, dual control,
decisions, the review queue, the one list, tenancy and tenant settings; Playform's own routes in
its `route-fixtures.app.test.ts`). The baseline is `{ count: 0, files: {} }` in both repositories
and the guard (`fake-fetch-bodies.test.ts`) asserts it stays so: any hand-written body fails.

- **The scanner sees more.** It counted a body only where written in the mock's call; a literal
  bound to a name first (`const body = {…}`, assigned later) or returned by a function in the
  same file was not counted. It follows both now (`fake-fetch-scan.ts`: `boundLiterals`,
  `reachedLiterals`, with a `[self-test]` that fails on the old scanner). On the base the new
  scanner counts 199 in 19 files here and 257 in 24 in Playform; now 0 and 0.
- **Real defects found** (each fixed, with a test that fails without the fix):
  - **The dual-control panel listed nothing.** It read `get_config`'s answer as `data.value`; the
    route answers `data.entry.value`, so against the real route the panel always said "No keys are
    dual-controlled." (`DualControlKeysPanel`; six of nine tests fail without the fix). The list is
    itself always dual-controlled, so the panel's "applied", two-person and lost-write branches
    were unreachable: removed, with `screens.dual_control.applied`.
  - **The Users panel claimed an erasure it cannot do, and dropped focus.** An erasure from the
    screen is always held (`ALWAYS_HELD_ACTIONS`); the tests answered 200 "completed" and
    "partial", and the panel's "erased" and "incomplete" branch was unreachable: removed (with
    `users.erased`, `users.erase_incomplete`). When the held note replaced the Erase button, focus
    fell to the page; it moves to the note now.
- **Tests that asserted answers no route sends** (each now the route's): a rate limit as
  `rate_limit.exceeded` (it is `rate.limited`), `run_failed` as 502 (503), a self-approval as 403
  with English and no code (409 `approvals.self_approval`), a review-queue claim conflict as
  "Already claimed" (`moderation.item_state_conflict`), `/api/admin/session` answering
  `account.not_found` (its guard cannot), an admin session opening no section (it always opens
  one), kill-switch answers without `withdrawn` and `republished`, MFA setup refused as 400 (501
  `feature.not_configured`), a renewed session for another user (refused `auth.token_invalid`),
  tenancy messages and statuses the operator routes never send, invented ids and readiness checks.
- **How fixtures are made:** the clock is frozen at `FIXTURE_NOW` while they are produced;
  generated ids are numbered per answer; request ids, alone or quoted in a message, are fixed.
  Only the stores beneath a route are stubbed; the guard, the permission lookup and the handler
  are real.

**N-107 — a duplicated role's note, and no answer shown as JSON.** Duplicating a role wrote
`'Duplicated from ' || $3 || '. ' || …` into its description: English the database stored and the
Roles screen showed in every locale. The note is now `roles.description_note`, a screen message's
key and values (migration 065, with a check that it is one); the description keeps what an
administrator wrote; `GET /api/admin/roles` answers `descriptionNote` and the Roles screen renders
it (`roleDescription`). Rows written before are migrated by 065 (documented in
MIGRATION_v5_to_v6; replayed twice in `migration-replay.sh`, a description written by hand left
alone). The guard: rule C of `screen-text-indirect` now reads SQL's string literals too (`sqlPhrases`,
`sqlWordSites`: app/api at 0; platform/ and lib/ hold ten known sites, listed with why, which
fail when one is added or goes), and a new rule D fails on a screen that shows an answer as
`JSON.stringify(…)` (Playform's agent console did, below).

**N-108 — a job failure recorded before codes.** A job's last error recorded before TASK-206 is
English the runner wrote. The Jobs screen no longer shows it as if it were the catalog's: such a
record shows `screens.jobs.errors.uncoded` ("A failure recorded before failures were coded."),
with the stored text behind a disclosure (`JobError`, `codedJobError`); a coded one shows its
catalog sentence. No migration: the stored text is the record and is kept. Walked at 390 px.

**Found by the walk at 390 px** (each on the base too; fixed, each with a test that fails without
it): the Jobs screen's three tables made the page 676 px wide — each now scrolls within its card;
and on the dual-control list (which now lists its keys) a long key pushed its Remove button past
the edge — the key wraps and the button keeps its size.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** the Roles screen and `GET /api/admin/roles`; the command bar's `duplicate_role`; the
  Jobs screen; the dual-control and Users panels; screen tests and their fixtures (no route's
  answer changes but `descriptionNote`, added).
- **Races:** none new. A duplicate writes its note in the statement that creates the role.
- **Dependencies down:** the database down: as before (500 `internal.error`). A note whose key the
  catalog lacks: the check refuses anything but a `screens.` key, and rule C checks every key a
  `shown(…)` names.
- **Erasure leftovers:** none new: the note holds a role's name, no person's data.
- **Screens × responses:** the Roles screen renders `descriptionNote`; the Jobs screen an uncoded
  failure; the dual-control panel reads `entry.value`. Every changed answer's fixture regenerated
  by its handler (the drift test failed on the roles answer until it was).
- **Journeys touched:** the admin console (walked at 1280 and 390 px, base and change), the Jobs
  screen at 390 px (navigation paced under the rate limiter); the PF e2e suite, spec by spec.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No. The catalog is the platform's (ADR-053 D5); a duplicate is
  still operator-only.

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** text from the database and the routes to an administrator's screen.
- **Actors that exist today:** the deployment's administrators and operators. None can do more
  with this change: a role's note is written by server code only (`shown(…)`), and the column's
  check refuses any other shape; a description an administrator writes is shown as written, as
  before. No actor today could exploit the defects fixed (the dual-control panel showed too
  little, never too much).
- **Bypasses:** a screen showing an answer as JSON (rule D), English written in a statement in
  app/api (rule C, SQL); a test asserting a body no route sends (the fake-fetch guard at 0, and
  fixture drift).
- **Forgeries:** none new: a note's key and values come from server code (the duplicate's source
  is the role read under the lock); a client cannot set `description_note` — no route writes it
  from input, and the column's check refuses any but a screen message's shape.
- **Legitimate flows:** duplicating, listing and viewing roles; listing jobs, an old failure still
  readable on request.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for sub-batch 55g (2026-11-09).

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** `roles` readers (the roles route, the command bar's search, which keeps
  `description`, and the catalog loaders that select by name); `RolesDataView`; every caller of
  `jobErrorText` (the console's three render sites); `DualControlKeysPanel`'s callers; the
  `fake-fetch-scan` readers (the guard, `process-check`'s baseline rule); fixture loaders in both
  repositories.
- **Hostile re-read:** a note with an English key (refused by the check, tested), a role whose
  description begins "Duplicated from" by hand (left alone, replayed), a JSON dump nested in a
  screen's text (rule D's self-test), a body bound to a name or returned by a helper (scanner
  self-test), a stored job error carrying markup (React escapes it; it is shown only on request).
- **Found and left (out of scope, reported):** SQL in platform/ that stores English notes (proposal
  decisions, an abandoned trajectory's reason, an erased note's placeholder, a carried-over ban's
  reason, the audit export's "the platform"): ten sites, listed in rule C's known list; the tenancy
  erasure label "Erase the account an account that is no longer found".

- **N-103 — one tenant directory.** A dedicated deployment (`TENANCY_MODE=single`) left
  `TENANT_DIRECTORY_STORE` unset and ran on the in-memory directory, while the tenant lifecycle is
  SQL on the owner connection (ADR-053 D7). An operator's new tenant, rename or address lived only
  in the process that made it; removing an address just added read `tenant_domains` and answered
  404, and a deletion read `tenants` and did not find the tenant (TASK-204's e2e journey found it).
  The directory is now the database's whenever there is one: unset means `postgres` with a
  `DATABASE_URL` (`getTenantDirectoryStore`, used by boot and readiness), and `memory` beside a
  database is refused by the environment contract in every mode, local and CI runs too (ADR-053
  A12; ENV_REFERENCE, TENANCY_OPERATIONS §2, `.env.example`). Journey:
  `__tests__/db/tenant-directory-single.db.test.ts` (boot's choice, then provision, add an
  address, remove it, rename, delete with a second operator, each read back from the database) and
  `e2e/admin-routes.spec.ts` (the address just mapped is removed; the tenant provisioned is deleted
  by two operators).
- **N-104 — a job run's whole record.** A manual run wrote `released`, `hung` and `stoppedBy` on
  its outcome record and the schema dropped them, logging "Audit details carried keys its
  action's schema does not allow". The caller is right (the record says what happened): the
  schema now allows them (`platform/auth/audit-details.ts`), and the route test runs the real
  writer on the record the run writes and asserts nothing is dropped or logged.
- **N-102 — API answers a screen shows come from the catalog.** A route's answer that a screen
  shows as words is a catalog key and values (`platform/errors/shown-text.ts`: `shown`,
  `renderShown`; a value may itself be one), rendered by the screen: every command-bar result
  (`app/api/admin/ai/handlers/*`: "Role changed to …", "Password policy updated", the search
  summaries, held changes), why a hold waits (`PendingApproval.reason`, a run's recorded note by
  its code's sentence or the store's own notes), the operator readiness checks and the identity
  provider's reasons, a job kind's description and its recorded failure (now a code:
  `reported`, `timeout:<ms>`, `sqlstate:<code>`…; a record from before is shown as recorded), an
  erased account's name in a search's table, the config agent's reply. Coded refusals' params
  carry ids, never words: `request.invalid_value` gained optional `expected` and `max` (a
  described value, worded by a `select`), `admin.target_not_found`'s `target` is an id, and an
  operator failure's reason is a token (`tenant.conflict` and `tenant.invalid` word it). Error
  codes are unchanged. `/api/health`'s `detail` is a code (ADR-056). Rule C of
  `__tests__/screen-text-indirect.test.ts` holds `app/api` at 0 (68 sites in PF and 69 in
  Playform on the base) and checks every key a `shown(…)` names; ADR-051 records it.
- **N-105 — one full stop.** `tenant.conflict` read "That could not be done: {reason}." with a
  sentence for the reason: "…awaiting approval..". Its reason is a token now, worded by the
  message; `__tests__/catalog-punctuation.test.ts` renders every message of every catalog in every

- **N-106 — the merged rules read once.** CLAUDE.md (both): the R-75/R-77 exceptions were stale

  directory conflict by `instanceof`; in a production build the directory boot installs

  the other bundle); the walk's second address answers 409 `tenant.conflict`.
- **Gitleaks.** gitleaks 8.28.0 (CI's pin) reports nothing in Playform's history: the fixture at
  `__tests__/agent-credential-routes.test.ts:54` (05eae13) is cleared by the content-and-path
  allowlist already in `.gitleaks.toml` (2bff5c5); with that allowlist removed it is reported, so
  the allowlist is what clears it. No change.

Walked: the admin console (Results, Approvals, Tenants and readiness, Jobs) on production builds
of the base and of this change, at 1280 px and 390 px.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** the command bar's execute route and its screen; the approvals listing and its panel;
  the operator readiness route and the Tenants screen; the Jobs console route and screen; every
  operator tenant route (their refusals' params); the routes that refuse with
  `request.invalid_value` or `admin.target_not_found` (params); `/api/health`'s `detail`; boot's
  directory and the environment contract; the audit schema of a manual job run.
- **Races:** none new. The directory change moves a dedicated deployment's reads onto the same
  tables its lifecycle already wrote under the tenant's lock; the cache (30 s) is cleared by each
  write as before.
- **Dependencies down:** the database down: the Postgres directory fails closed as in a shared
  deployment (a request's tenant cannot be read: 503); a dedicated deployment with no database at
  all keeps the in-memory directory. The catalog missing a key: the screen shows the key (the guard
  fails first).
- **Erasure leftovers:** none new: what is stored is codes in place of sentences (a job's last
  error, a command-bar change's comment is the catalog's rendering).
- **Screens × responses:** every changed answer has its screen moved with it: ExecutionResultsPanel
  (results, cells), HeldActionsPanel (reason), TenancyPanels (readiness), JobsPanels (description,
  failures); a refusal is still the registry's message. Fixtures regenerated by their handlers.
- **Journeys touched:** the admin console (walked), the operator tenant journey (e2e: address
  removed, tenant deleted), the dedicated deployment's boot.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No. A dedicated deployment's directory becomes the database's
  (the shared deployment's already was); refusals keep their codes and statuses.

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** text from the server to an administrator's or operator's screen; where a dedicated
  deployment keeps its tenants. Actors that exist: the deployment's administrators and operators,
  its users (whose input a reason could echo), the owner who configures the deployment.
- **Bypasses:** English reaching a screen through a field the guard cannot see (a platform module
  building an answer outside `app/api`): the fields screens render are typed `ShownText`, so the
  compiler refuses a string there; a reason echoing a typed host stays a bounded value
  (`echoed`), placed by the catalog.
- **Forgeries:** none new: a token or key comes from server code; a client cannot set one.
- **Legitimate flows:** every result, hold, check and job still shown, in the same words or the
  catalog's; an operator's provisioning, address and deletion steps now each see the last.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for sub-batch 55f (2026-11-08).

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** `ActionResult.result` (handlers, execute route, command bar, page,
  panel, the users-search handoff), `PendingApproval.reason` (panel, operator holds),
  `ReadinessCheck.detail` and the provider readiness types (both Cognito implementations, the
  mock), `describeUnapprovable`, `describeJobError` (runner, stores, console), `OperatorResult`
  (`message` → `reason`: tenancy, erasure attestation, the purge duty, operator-http, the export
  route), `TENANT_CONFLICT_REASON`, `request.invalid_value` (every caller passing a described
  value), `SERVER_SET_INPUTS`, `TABLE_NAMES`, the health route; tests moved with each.
- **Hostile re-read:** a key that does not exist (guard), a doubled stop in any branch (test), a
  megabyte host echoed (bounded, tested), `memory` beside a database in CI (refused, tested).

  who pushes), his agents, Dependabot, the model, and the running system's users.
- **Bypasses:** a pull request whose diff carries instructions to the reviewer (the diff is data in

  model answer carrying unsafe text past `/api/process` or `/api/identify` (screened — tests); a
  live eval passing without a key (it fails, saying so); a gate passing on nothing (each `[self-test]`).
- **Forgeries:** a Dependabot run without secrets mistaken for a pass (it warns, named); a stale
  model exception kept by hand (refused). Anything needing a second person with write access is out
  of scope: no such actor exists.
- **Legitimate flows:** a pull request reviewed and commented on; the weekly live eval; the hourly
  health watch opening and closing its issue; a sync after the promotion, once its guard proceeds; a
  translation and an identification answered as before when the screening passes.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for sub-batch 55d (2026-11-08): fix every item, kill
  the survivors, replace the action before 2026-12-31, make the sync idempotent, re-enable it only
  after the promotion.

### FEAT-090 — Admin-authored workflow composition (governed)

| Field          | Detail                                       |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**         | FEAT-090                                     |
| **Type**       | Feature — agent governance                   |
| **Severity**   | Enhancement                                  |
| **Component**  | platform/agents (run loop), admin governance |
| **Status**     | Deferred — revisit after Sprint 3c UX        |
| **Logged**     | 2026-08-31 (Sprint 3c UX)                    |
| **Resolve by** | Own ADR before build                         |

**What:** Let an admin compose a new workflow from EXISTING step primitives (goal,
description, ordered step intents, cost estimates, required capability, endpoint) through the
governance admin, without new per-workflow code. Raised during Sprint 3c UX (U2): capabilities
are derived from the code-registered workflow registry, so U2 shipped read-only — but the
question is whether workflows themselves could become admin-governed.

**Viability (assessed):** the execution model supports it. Steps run generically through
`invokeTool` keyed off the step-level `intent` (ADR-030 D1), not a per-goal switch — so a
workflow assembled from existing intents would run with no new step code.

**Why it is NOT a small change (the honest scope):**

1. PF's run loop reads workflows only from the code-populated registry (`registerWorkflow`).
   Admin-authored workflows require the loop to MERGE an authored-workflow governed store
   (config or table) with the code-registered definitions.
2. Consumers (not PF) register workflows and own their endpoints, so the authoring panel and
   the invocation/endpoint path are consumer-side — this spans both repos.
3. A composed workflow is EXECUTABLE AUTHORITY: an admin assembling "invoke tool X then Y"
   authors something with real effects. It needs a safety model — which tools a composed
   workflow may invoke, under what risk tier, and whether authoring itself needs approval.

**Resolution plan:**

1. Write an ADR for admin-authored workflow composition (the safety model is the crux:
   what may a composed workflow invoke, and under what governance).
2. PF: merge an authored-workflow store into the run-loop registry read.
3. Consumer: the authoring governance panel + the invocation path for authored workflows.
4. Remove this entry when delivered.

| Field          | Detail                                                  |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**         | FEAT-091                                                |
| **Type**       | Feature — GenAI control plane (GENAI_MANIFESTO §5, P13) |

| **Component**  | prompts/, platform/ai (orchestrator), admin governance  |
| **Status**     | Planned — not built                                     |

| **Resolve by** | Own ADR before build (ADR-017 surface 9, GENAI_ROADMAP) |

**What:** GENAI_MANIFESTO §5 called A/B testing and canary rollouts "first-class capabilities"; no
code implements them (a prompt or model change ships to every caller at once). Until this is
built, a change is held by the deterministic eval lane in CI and the keyed live lane
(`npm run eval:live`, ADR-038) — the manifesto and its readiness table now say so (P5 and P13
Partial). **Scope for the ADR:** a governed split (by tenant, cohort or percentage) between two
registered prompt versions or model tiers; the live lane's assertions as the comparison; a
canary that widens on its own only while the error and refusal rates hold; every split
recorded in the trajectory and the metrics, so a result can be attributed to its arm.

### CI-001 — GitHub Actions Node.js 24 deprecation warning

| Field          | Detail                                               |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**         | CI-001                                               |
| **Type**       | External dependency                                  |
| **Severity**   | Warning only — not a failure                         |
| **Component**  | actions/checkout, actions/setup-node                 |
| **Status**     | Open — UNBLOCKED, compatible versions have shipped   |
| **Logged**     | 2026-03-19                                           |
| **Resolve by** | 2026-09-16 (Node 20 removed from runners) — Sprint 1 |

**What:** Our workflows pin action majors that still run on Node.js 20
(checkout v4.2.2, setup-node v4.4.0, upload-artifact v4, codeql-action v3).
Node 24 became the default runtime on 2026-06-02; **Node 20 is removed from
GitHub runners on 2026-09-16**, after which these actions stop working.

**Unblocked (verified 2026-07-12):** Node 24-compatible majors have shipped —
`actions/checkout` v6/v7, `actions/setup-node` v6, `actions/upload-artifact` v5+/v7,
`github/codeql-action` v4. Dependabot has already opened PRs for checkout 7.0.0
and upload-artifact 7.0.1.

**Resolution plan:**

1. Bump the action majors in both repos, keeping the SHA-pin + `# vX` comment convention
2. Verify each workflow still passes (ci, codeql, semgrep, load-test, zap-scan, sync)
3. Drop the `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24` shim once everything is on Node 24
4. Remove this entry

**Close when:** no workflow runs a Node 20 action; no deprecation warning in CI output.

**Migrated from:** SECURITY_DEBT.md (Sprint 3c — not security-related)

### TASK-046 — Auth-enable k6 + live moderation/agent re-baseline

| Field        | Detail                                                                        |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**       | TASK-046                                                                      |
| **Type**     | Testing infrastructure / performance baseline                                 |
| **Severity** | Medium                                                                        |
| **Phase**    | Phase 5, Sprint 7 (phase-exit expectation)                                    |
| **Target**   | v6.x (re-targeted 2026-11-08 from "Phase 5, Sprint 7", closed: TASK-204 N-12) |
| **Status**   | Open                                                                          |
| **Logged**   | 2026-06-21                                                                    |
| **Source**   | Phase 5 Sprint 0 k6 re-baseline finding                                       |

**What:** `k6/api-load.js`'s `DRY_RUN=0` ("live, ~$5") profile is stale — it predates
Sprint 3d, which added `requireAuthWithStatus` to `/api/process` (and, in Playform, guarded `/api/stream` — in platform-foundation that route was unguarded until TASK-133). The
script sends no auth header, so every live request 401s at the guard before reaching
moderation, translate/classify, or the orchestrator. A live run today costs ~$0 and
measures only 401-rejection latency.

**Resolution:** add auth to the k6 script — since TASK-214 (ADR-057) a user route takes only the
cookie session, so: sign in once per virtual user (`POST /api/auth/sign-in`, k6's cookie jar keeps
the session cookie), read the session's forgery token (`GET /api/auth/session`, `csrfToken`), and
send it as `x-csrf-token` with the deployment's own `Origin` on the `/process` and `/stream`
calls (never an `Authorization: Bearer` header — no route reads one from a user). Then run `DRY_RUN=0` against **staging** for the first real
moderation + agent latency baseline. Phase-exit expectation — do not close Phase 5 without it.

**Dry baseline (Phase 5 Sprint 0, for reference):** prod, 10 VUs, 1221 reqs, 0% errors;
process p95 76.9ms, stream p95 71.4ms, health p95 149ms (health p99 tripped on a single ~2s
Vercel cold start).
