### TASK-201 — Deadlines before 2027: runner images pinned, Supabase secret keys, the security-review action re-checked

| Field        | Detail                                                                                  |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**       | TASK-201                                                                                |
| **Type**     | Defect (CI runner drift; a retiring credential; a third-party action's pinned model)    |
| **Severity** | High (every CI job moved at once by GitHub; Supabase deletes the legacy keys late 2026) |
| **Phase**    | Phase 5                                                                                 |
| **Target**   | v6.0.0 (RC)                                                                             |
| **Status**   | Fixed on develop (sub-batch 55a of the residuals batch); owner steps below              |
| **Logged**   | 2026-11-07 (the rebuilt residuals register: S2-C1, N-76, N-79)                          |

Three items with dates outside our control, fixed together in both repositories.

**1. Runner images (S2-C1).** Every job ran on `ubuntu-latest`, which GitHub began moving to Ubuntu
26.04 on 2026-10-19, and the Postgres 17 + pgvector step built its apt source from
`$(lsb_release -cs)`, so on the new image it would ask apt.postgresql.org for a release it may not
publish — Layer 1, the migration replay, the container image job and Playform's E2E all depend on
that step. Now every job (17 in platform-foundation, 22 in Playform, and the sync template) runs on
`ubuntu-24.04`; the apt source names `${PGDG_CODENAME}-pgdg` from the step's
`PGDG_CODENAME: noble`, and the step fails first, saying which, when the runner's
`VERSION_CODENAME` (`/etc/os-release`) differs or apt.postgresql.org does not publish that release
(a retried `curl -I` of its `Release` file). `workflow-hygiene` gains two guards: `runnerProblems`
(a `-latest` label, an expression, no `runs-on`, a label list or group, or any image but
`RUNNER_IMAGE`) and `pgdgProblems` (an apt source read from the runner, a `PGDG_CODENAME` other than
`RUNNER_CODENAME`, or no check against the runner), each with a `[self-test]` planting every case.

**2. Supabase secret keys (N-76).** Supabase is "deprecating the `anon` and `service_role` keys by
the end of 2026" ([API keys](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/api-keys)); creating new keys
does not revoke the legacy ones, which are disabled separately
([migrating to the new API keys](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/migrating-to-new-api-keys)).
A secret key (`sb_secret_…`) is not a JWT, reaches the data as the `service_role` role and is sent
"on the `apikey` header, not on `Authorization: Bearer`" (both pages, read 2026-11-07). The
migration parity check sent the legacy JWT as both headers. Now:

- `scripts/migration-parity.mjs` reads `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, refuses a value that is not a secret
  key (a JWT, a publishable key) before any request, sends it as `apikey` only, and answers a 401
  or 403 as "the key was refused" (exit 2, cannot check — never drift). A run with only
  `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` stops, naming the new variable. A clean cut, no transition: the old
  variable is never sent.
- `.github/workflows/migration-parity.yml` passes `secrets.SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`; an environment
  with only one of `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` fails, naming the other (whatever
  `MIGRATION_PARITY_REQUIRED` says) — so an environment still holding only the legacy secret fails
  rather than skipping; one with neither still skips with a notice (platform-foundation, which sets
  neither today).
- The environment contract declares `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` (shape `sb_secret_` and 16 or more of
  `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), required with `REALTIME_PROVIDER=supabase`; `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is no
  longer declared or shaped, and set alone with Realtime on Supabase the violation names the new
  variable. No code path sends a Supabase key (Realtime takes its client from the app), so nothing
  else moves.
- ENV_REFERENCE, the providers README, ASSURANCE §4, TENANCY_OPERATIONS §1.4, `.env.example` and
  both credential registers name the new key.

**3. The security-review action (N-79, S3-E13).** Re-checked on 2026-11-07:
`anthropics/claude-code-security-review` has no tag or release (`git ls-remote --tags`: none), and
the pin `0c6a49f1fa56a1d472575da86a94dbc1edb78eda` is still the head of its `main`, so there is no
newer commit to pin. In that source the scan's model is `DEFAULT_CLAUDE_MODEL =
os.environ.get('CLAUDE_MODEL') or 'claude-opus-4-1-20250805'` (`claudecode/constants.py:8`), and
`action.yml:189` sets `CLAUDE_MODEL` from the `claude-model` input, which the workflow already sets
to the registry's standard model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`); only `validate_api_access` keeps the
hard-coded `claude-3-5-haiku-20241022` (`claude_api_client.py:62`) — the known exception, unchanged,
review-by 2026-12-31. Found doing this: with the action's full file list (CI reads it with the job's
token) the model check failed on the default in `constants.py`, which no exception recorded — run
here against the action's real source served locally, the old script exits 1. The exception now
records that default as `overridden` by `claude-model`, and the check requires the step using the
action to set that input (`stepInput`); a step without it fails, naming the input.

**Owner steps** (in order; each with its check). Supabase: create a secret key per project
(Settings → API Keys → "Publishable and secret API keys" → Create new API keys); set it as the
`SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` secret of the GitHub Environments `staging` and `production` in each
repository that runs the parity check (Playform; platform-foundation has none to set), through a
hidden prompt; promote, then run the parity workflow by hand and see it read the database (its
output lists the comparison; a refused key says so); only then delete the old
`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` secrets, remove `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` from any Vercel project that
still has it, and, at the end of the promotion, deactivate the legacy keys in Supabase (Settings →
API Keys; reversible). The security-review action: before 2026-12-31, decide whether to replace it,
remove it, or extend the exception — no upstream commit fixes the validation model.

**Playform.** The same shared files byte for byte; its own workflows (22 jobs, four Postgres
steps, the parity workflow), credential register, LIVE_JOURNEY_CHECK §10, migration guide and
release notes — Playform TASK-5002 in `docs/PLAYFORM_TASKS.md`.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** CI and the operator's tools only. The workflows' runner and Postgres step, the parity
  script (run by the parity workflow against the live databases, read-only), the model check, and
  the environment contract, which a deployment reads at boot — only for `REALTIME_PROVIDER=supabase`,
  which no deployment selects today. No route, screen, role, agent or guest path changes.
- **Races:** none. Each CI job installs its own Postgres; the parity check reads one table per
  environment; two runs share nothing but read-only requests.
- **Dependencies down:** apt.postgresql.org unreachable or without the release: the step fails
  before installing, saying so. Supabase refusing the key: exit 2 "the key was refused", never
  drift. The action's source unreadable: unverifiable, as before (a failure).
- **Erasure leftovers:** none: nothing is stored. The parity check reads file names and checksums,
  no person's data.
- **Screens × responses:** no screen changes; no route answers differently. The contract's
  violation text changes for a Realtime-on-Supabase deployment without the new key.
- **Journeys touched:** none: no page or route changes, and `journey-exemptions.json` is unchanged.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No: the parity check keeps every comparison and fails on a
  missing key where it used to skip only when the URL was absent too; the runner guard and the model
  check only add refusals; the contract still requires a key where Realtime needs one.

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** the CI workflows of both repositories (every job's runner image, the Postgres step,
  the model check, the parity workflow) and the parity check's credential, between a change and
  `develop`, `staging` and `main`. The actors that exist: the owner (the only account that pushes or
  merges, with 2FA), by hand or through an AI agent; Dependabot; GitHub, which moves `-latest`
  labels on its own schedule; Supabase, which retires the legacy keys.
- **Bypasses** (our own mistakes): a job added on `ubuntu-latest`, a runner from an expression, or
  the image changed without the apt source (the runner guards, and the step itself); a key sent as a
  Bearer token or printed (refused shapes are never sent; no message carries a value — tests); a
  parity run passing on nothing because only the old secret is set (it fails, naming the new one);
  the action's default model silently used (the step must set `claude-model`).
- **Forgeries:** none in scope: each needs an actor who does not exist for these repositories (a
  second author editing a workflow or a secret); out of scope, not a residual.
- **Legitimate flows:** a push or pull request running every layer on `ubuntu-24.04`; the weekly
  and dispatched parity runs, with credentials (Playform) or without (platform-foundation, skipped
  with a notice); Dependabot's bumps (no secrets: unchanged); the weekly model check, with the full
  file list (token) or without it (only the recorded file).
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for sub-batch 55a (2026-11-07): pin `ubuntu-24.04` and
  the codename with a guard; re-pin the action to its latest release or set `claude-model` and say
  so; a clean cut to `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `apikey` only, with owner steps.

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** every reader of `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (`git grep`): the parity
  script, its workflow, the contract and its tests, `rate-limit-registry.test.ts`, ENV_REFERENCE,
  the providers README, ASSURANCE, TENANCY_OPERATIONS, `.env.example`, the credential registers;
  the historical migration guides and ADRs are records and keep the old name. Every `runs-on`
  (`grep -c`: 17 and 22 jobs, one template) and every apt source of apt.postgresql.org (3 and 4);
  `credential-register.test.ts` (every secret a workflow reads has a row); `check-model-ids`'s
  other callers (the model-registry workflow only).
- **Hostile re-read:** tried to get past each change: `ubuntu-latest` in a label list, `${{
matrix.os }}`, `runs-on: { group: … }`, `ubuntu-22.04`, a job with no `runs-on`; an apt source with
  `$(lsb_release -cs)`, a literal `noble`, `PGDG_CODENAME: resolute`, no runner check — each refused
  by a self-test, and each guard seen failing on a planted `ubuntu-latest` and `lsb_release` in the
  real workflows; the parity script with the Bearer header restored and with the shape check off —
  its tests fail; a JWT, a publishable key or a truncated key under the new name — refused, never
  sent, never printed; the model check with a `claude-model` only on a later step, or set to a
  non-registry model — refused. The changed shell steps were run here (see the batch notes): the
  codename check on this Ubuntu 24.04 host passes and on a faked `resolute` fails with its message;
  the parity step's branches run with each combination of secrets.

### TASK-202 — The admin console made usable: edit settings, decide approvals seeing what changes, people by address, results that stay, forms for agents and erasures

| Field        | Detail                                                                                      |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**       | TASK-202                                                                                    |
| **Type**     | Defect (the admin console could not be used by a person without code)                       |
| **Severity** | High (an approver decided changes blind; a setting could only be changed from a console)    |
| **Phase**    | Phase 5                                                                                     |
| **Target**   | v6.0.0 (RC)                                                                                 |
| **Status**   | Fixed on develop (sub-batch 55b of the residuals batch)                                     |
| **Logged**   | 2026-11-07 (the owner's first walk through the console: N-60 to N-66, N-69; S3-E19, S3-E21) |

The owner walked the console on 2026-11-07 and could not do the job on it: Platform config could
only search (he changed a setting from the browser console); Approvals showed a tool's name and a
requester's id, so he approved blind; a decision's result vanished after six seconds and read
"update_config…"; people were named by raw ids ("User c408… assigned", audit actors and targets,
requesters, per-account blocks); tables ran past the window and cut values with "…" and no way to
read them; one search returned three unrelated tables; Trusted agents had no form; no screen showed
an erasure waiting on the two-operator attestation. Every test passed: none asked whether a person
could complete the task on screen. Fixed, each on the governed path that already existed:

- **N-60 — Platform config edits a setting.** `components/admin/PlatformConfigPanel.tsx` lists every
  setting (`GET /api/admin/config?enhanced=true`), filtered on the screen; a row opens its panel —
  key, what it does, tier (and who may change it), type, current value, platform default, range or
  allowed values, last change — and an edit form read by the setting's type (`config-value.ts`: an
  on/off switch, a number checked against its range, a choice of its allowed values, a JSON list
  checked before it is sent) with a required comment. It submits `update_config`, confirmed, to
  `POST /api/admin/config-ai/execute`, as the Dual control panel does; the result says
  "Applied: … is now …" or "Held for approval by <a safety approver or super admin | an
  administrator or super admin> other than you", and stays until dismissed. An admin without the
  tier's permission (`config_manage_standard`, `config_manage_safety` — the route's own rule) sees
  no edit button and is told which permission it needs.
- **N-61 — Approvals show what is decided.** `GET /api/admin/approvals` now answers, per hold:
  `requestedBy` — the requester (the person an agent acted for: `actor.onBehalfOf`, else the actor)
  resolved to address and role in the tenant's transaction (`platform/admin/account-names.ts`), or
  `erased` / `unknown`, never an id; `change` — a config change's key, value now (the hold's
  recorded `heldPrevious`, an approval's `currentValue`) and after, scope and action; `comment` —
  the requester's change comment. `change` and `comment` go only to a viewer who could decide the
  hold, as the summary already did (round 2, N2). The command bar's summaries now also name a role
  action's role and the permissions it grants or takes away (`permissionsGranted`,
  `permissionsRemoved`: catalog codes only, read from the database — a role change's from the two
  roles), an entitlement group's code and on/off. The panel (`HeldActionsPanel.tsx`) shows one card
  per hold: what (a setting's key with now → after, a list's added and removed items; an account by
  address with its role from → to and the permissions; an erasure's account), who asked (address
  and role), when, their reason, who may approve; Approve and Reject each open a confirm step that
  repeats what and who. Tenant scoping, the permission checks and the approver rules are unchanged.
- **N-62 — Results stay and name the change.** `ResultList.tsx`: every change and decision on these
  screens lists its result — applied, held for approval (by whom), or not done (the catalog's
  reason) — named by what changed, never a tool's id, until its own Dismiss. A decision's 200 says
  whether it applied (`applied`, `pendingApproval`; a two-person approval's 200 is its apply), and
  `refusedDecisionText` takes the hold's words (`what`) while keeping its rules by tool.
- **N-63 — People by address.** Each place a grep of `components/admin`, `app/admin` and the
  handlers found (ids cut with `slice(0, 8)` or `slice(0, 12)`, `requester`, `actorId`, `user_id`,
  `created_by`, results built from an id):
  the role-change result ("User <id> assigned to …") and the restriction results ("… for user
  <id>") — now "Role changed to …" with the account by address beside it (`ActionResult.account`,
  added by the execute route for the screen only, never in the recorded step); the audit log's actor
  and target (`GET /api/admin/audit` names each; the search tool's audit rows gain `actor` and
  `target`, `withAccountNames`, screen only); the approvals requester; the per-account blocks'
  account and blocker (`GET /api/admin/per-account`); the confirm step's account
  (`POST /api/admin/ai` answers `accounts`, by action, for actions the admin may run); a summary
  target without an address ("Account: u-2"); the operators' tenant settings, whose held changes
  named the requester and the tool by id (`TenancyPanels.tsx`, from the same listing, read in the
  target tenant). An id is shown only as a detail (Show details, or an id that names no account).
- **N-64 — Tables fit.** The shell is a sidebar from `md` up and a section picker on a phone; the
  content never widens the page (`min-w-0`); every table scrolls in its own panel; a cut value has a
  "Show all" button (`ExpandableText.tsx`) instead of a tooltip a touch screen never shows. Checked
  at 1280 px and 390 px by the E2E walk (no horizontal page scroll).
- **N-65 — A search reads its screen.** `app/api/admin/ai/search-scope.ts`: the planner's searches
  of tables outside the section's own are dropped unless the request names the table, and the plan
  says which (`scopedOut`); Platform config's own filter reads nothing from the server.
- **N-66 — Trusted agents has forms.** `TrustedAgentsPanel.tsx`: register (id, owner, scope, token
  ceiling), edit scope or ceiling (one change at a time — each is held and approved on its own),
  suspend or reactivate after a confirm, each through `POST /api/admin/ai/execute` with one
  `register_agent` / `set_agent_scope` / `set_agent_ttl` / `suspend_agent` action; held or applied,
  said and kept.
- **S3-E19 — Erasures.** `GET /api/operator/erasures` (operators: `platform_operate`;
  `platform/gdpr/erasure-status.ts`, owner transaction purpose `operator`, read-only) lists every
  open erasure across tenants — its data purge, each external step (done, attempts,
  `poolUnverified`), an open attestation request and who asked, an attestation that closed it — and
  the operators who could attest; the Erasures section (after Approvals) shows them and asks,
  approves or rejects the attestation on the existing route. When no operator other than the
  requester exists it says "No eligible second operator: see single-owner dual control" and offers
  no request no one could approve. The attestation rules are unchanged (sub-batch 55c's).
- **S3-E21 — Dead panels deleted.** `AdminConfigPanels.tsx`, `AdminDataPanels.tsx` and
  `AdminPasswordPanel.tsx` were imported and tested nowhere (and duplicated live panels): deleted,
  with their coverage-ignore entries; so was `PlatformConfigDataView`, exported and used nowhere.
- **N-69 — The usability lens.** REVIEW.md rule 25 (a fourth lens for a screen: complete the task on
  screen, see what is decided, people by address, results that stay, fits 1280 and 390 px) and
  CLAUDE.md's handover: an admin change is walked in a browser on a production build first.

Every new word on these screens is in `messages/en.json`; the screen-literal baseline falls from 312
to 232 (Playform 350 to 270). E2E: `e2e/admin-console.spec.ts` walks the fixed flows as two
administrators on the production build and the replayed database — Playform's CI runs it
(TASK-5001); platform-foundation's CI runs no Playwright job (a workflow change, outside this
sub-batch), so its copy is the same file, run in Playform. The test double gains two administrators
(`MOCK_EXTRA_IDENTITIES`, refused off the ci and local hosts as the whole provider is).

Not done here, found on the way (filed for their batches): S3-E20 — the admin console's main files
are still excluded from coverage (`package.json` `coveragePathIgnorePatterns`); the approvals list's
"why held" text is still built in English on the server (`pending-approvals.ts` `reason`); the
command bar's `assigned`-style results of other handlers (agents' "Registered agent <id>") name an
agent, not a person, and stay.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** admins of a tenant (the approvals list: `can_access_admin`; config edits: the key's
  tier permission; agents: `admin_manage_agents`; per-account: `admin_manage_account_restrictions`;
  audit: `admin_view_audit`), operators (`platform_operate`: the erasures list and the attestation),
  the command bar's planner and executor. Guests, users without an admin role and agents reach none
  (the guards are unchanged; the new route is `requireAdmin(…, "platform_operate")`). The mock
  provider's two new identities exist only where the test double runs (ci, local).
- **Races:** a hold decided while a viewer reads the list: the decision route is unchanged (409 as
  before), and the panel reads the list again when the answer says the row changed. A setting
  changed between opening the panel and submitting: the governed write validates and records
  against the value it finds, and a held change applies only onto the value it was held against
  (review 12 H2, unchanged). Names are read after the rows: an account erased in between is named as
  erased or not found, never by id.
- **Dependencies down:** the names read fails: rows are listed with `requestedBy: unknown` and no
  account names (never an id, never a failed list); the erasures read fails: a coded 500 and the
  panel's "could not be read" (no partial list); the config re-read after a change fails: the result
  says so and that the list may show the old value; the planner's account read fails: the plan is
  answered without names (the confirm shows what was asked, as before).
- **Erasure leftovers:** nothing new is stored. Names are read at request time from `users` (an
  erased account has no address, so it is named "erased"); the recorded step of a command-bar action
  keeps the id in its input as before and gains no address (the account is added to the screen's
  copy only); the audit search's address columns are the screen's only (`searchStepRecord` keeps
  ids and counts).
- **Screens × responses:** `GET /api/admin/approvals` (+ `requestedBy`, `change`, `comment`;
  callers: HeldActionsPanel; TenancyPanels through `GET /api/operator/tenants/[id]/approvals`, the
  same listing; the planner's context — unchanged fields only, no viewer: no names);
  `GET /api/admin/audit` (+ `actor`, `target`: AuditDataView); `GET /api/admin/per-account`
  (+ `user`, `created_by_account`: PerAccountRestrictionsDataView); `POST /api/admin/ai`
  (+ `plan.scopedOut`, `plan.accounts`: ActionConfirmPanel via app/admin/page.tsx);
  `POST /api/admin/ai/execute` (+ `results[].account`, audit rows' `actor`/`target` columns, the
  role and restriction result texts without ids: ExecutionResultsPanel, TrustedAgentsPanel, the
  Users screen's hand-off reads only search tables); `GET /api/operator/erasures` (new:
  ErasuresPanel); the attestation route (unchanged: ErasuresPanel);
  `POST /api/admin/config-ai/execute` (unchanged: PlatformConfigPanel, DualControlKeysPanel);
  `POST /api/admin/approvals/[id]` (unchanged: HeldActionsPanel, TenancyPanels'
  `refusedDecisionText`, the page's planned decision). Every caller routes refusals through
  `readRefusal` (`refusal-coverage` passes with no new gap).
- **Journeys touched:** the admin console (`/admin`) and its sections — Platform config, Approvals,
  Trusted agents, Erasures, Audit log, Per-account, the command bar's confirm and results; the E2E
  walk covers `/admin`, the session, config, config assistant, approvals, agent registry, command
  bar, audit and erasures routes and the attestation route (journey exemptions 74 → 65; Playform
  56 → 52); Playform's live Journey C reads Platform config and Erasures too.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No. No permission, guard, approver rule, tenant scope or
  attestation rule changes; the new values go to the viewers the summary already went to (a hold's
  values and comment only to one who could decide it); names are read in the tenant's own
  transaction, so another tenant's account is never named; the erasures read is operators' only.
  Tested: a non-decider sees no values or comment; another tenant's account is not named; a tenant
  admin is refused the erasures read.

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** the admin and operator API routes this changes (approvals list, audit, per-account,
  the planner and executor, the new erasures read) and the test double's identities, between a
  signed-in administrator or operator and the tenant's data. Actors that exist: the owner (the only
  person who pushes), his agents, the running system's administrators, operators and users, and the
  tenants.
- **Bypasses:** reading another tenant's names through a hold or audit row naming its ids (names are
  read under row-level security — test); a non-decider reading a held change's values (`decider`
  gate — test); a tenant admin reading erasures across tenants (`platform_operate` — test); an id in
  another spelling escaping the "own request" or "requester" checks (`sameId` — tests); the planner
  naming an account for an action the admin may not run (`holds` check — test); the mock identities
  reaching a deployment (the environment contract refuses the mock provider off ci/local, ADR-050
  D1 — unchanged).
- **Forgeries:** a crafted `requester` or `actor` in a hold cannot choose a name: names come only
  from `users` by id or subject in the tenant; a client cannot send `scopedOut` or `accounts` to the
  executor (they are the planner's answer, display only; the executor checks every action again).
  Forgeries needing an actor who does not exist (a second author of the code) are out of scope.
- **Legitimate flows:** an admin changes a standard setting (applied) and a dual-controlled one
  (held); a second admin approves it, seeing key, values, requester and reason; an admin registers,
  edits and suspends an agent; an operator asks for an attestation and a second operator approves
  it; a single-owner deployment sees why no second operator can; every screen at 1280 px and 390 px.
- **Agreed before code:** written from the owner's brief for sub-batch 55b (2026-11-07: the ten
  items, the governed paths to use, "do not change the attestation rules"); no commit exists before
  this entry, and the owner reviews it with the change before it is committed.

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** every caller of the changed responses (the list in Screens × responses);
  `refusedDecisionText`'s two callers (HeldActionsPanel, TenancyPanels — the old signature still
  works); `heldActionSummary`'s consumers (the approvals list; `heldTargetAccount` in the decision
  route — unchanged); the tests that asserted the old texts and layout (shell, sign-out, confirm,
  results, search grid, approvals, summaries, eligibility, the audit route, the route matrix, the
  live journeys' "Admin Panel" and "Sign Out" in Playform); the dead files' references
  (`platform-paths.json`, `package.json`); both repositories' baselines (screen literals down,
  journey exemptions down, fake-fetch unchanged — the new screen tests answer from route fixtures
  produced by the real handlers).
- **Hostile re-read:** tried to see a value or comment as a non-decider (refused by the `decider`
  gate — test); to name another tenant's account through an audit row and a hold (null — test); to
  get an address into a recorded step (the account is added after `runCommandBarAction` returns;
  `stepRecordOf` unchanged); to make the panel show an id when names fail (`unknown`, test); to make
  "own request" miss an upper-case id or a subject (`sameId` — test; a non-UUID subject in another
  case is another operator, as `sameId` rules); to pass a JSON object to a list setting, a number
  out of range, an empty comment (refused before sending — tests; the server validates again); a
  search scoped out by a lookalike word ("auditor", "settingsx": not names — test); the section key
  "constructor" (`hasOwnProperty` — test); the browser's own validation bubble hiding the panel's
  reasons (`noValidate`, found by the test). Found by walking it on the production build and fixed:
  a requester's role shown as stored ("Super Admin", now read as the Users screen reads one); the
  console's header naming the role by its id ("super_admin"); "why held" in the server's own terms
  ("Held at effectiveRisk "restricted" (effects: stateWrite)", now the catalog's words, the detail
  behind Details); the audit log's action broken mid-word.

### TASK-205 — Caught-error text logged, never returned; every screen literal in the catalog

| Field        | Detail                                                                                              |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**       | TASK-205                                                                                            |
| **Type**     | Defect (internal text reached results, records and answers; English on screens outside the catalog) |
| **Severity** | High (R-75 and R-77 were Important; R-78 Low)                                                       |
| **Phase**    | Phase 5                                                                                             |
| **Target**   | v6.0.0 (RC)                                                                                         |
| **Status**   | Fixed on develop (sub-batch 55e of the residuals batch)                                             |
| **Logged**   | 2026-11-06 (sweep 4: S4-C1, S4-C2, S4-C3 — register N-57, N-58, N-59; residuals R-75, R-77, R-78)   |

Three residuals of TASK-194 rounds 14 and 15, open since:

- **R-77 (N-58) — a caught error's text left its catch.** `__tests__/error-text-not-returned.test.ts`
  scanned only `platform/admin`, `app/api` and `lib/`; the rest of `platform/` held 118 sites where
  `err.message`, `String(err)` or `${err}` went into a result, a stored record, a thrown error's
  reason, a health answer or a metric. Some reached people: the audit log's failed-act `reason`
  (read on the admin console), erasure results and their external-store outcomes, the moderation
  queue's restore and strike messages, approvals' `lastRunError`, `/api/health` details, a RAG
  answer's explanation; the rest reached logs only by way of a field. Each site now logs the text
  where it is caught, with its context, and carries a fixed text or a code
  (`platform/observability/caught-error.ts`: `logCaught`, `failedWrite`, `WRITE_FAILED`,
  `READ_FAILED`, `CALL_FAILED`, `PROBE_FAILED`). Where a caller acted on the text, it now acts on a
  type: the age route answers `account.age_already_recorded` from the result's `errorCode` (it
  matched English: `startsWith("the age is already recorded")`); the delete route's "no such user"
  comes from a typed error; a relink report names which stamps were not published from
  `NotPublishedError.parts`; a run's own refusal text travels as a field this module wrote
  (`RelinkUsageError.usage`, `ChangedMeanwhile.detail`, `RestoreFailure.reason`,
  `ValkeyUrlError.violation`, `TENANT_CONFLICT_TEXT` by code), never as another error's message. A
  database probe's own timeout still says "did not answer within N ms" (`DatabaseProbeTimeout`). AI
  failure metrics record the failure's class (`refused`, `transient: overloaded`, `error`).
  `errorMessage()` (provider-health), a helper that returned an error's text, is gone.
- **R-78 (N-59) — the diagnostic was lost.** Playform's export and erasure module turned a failure
  into `err.message` through a helper (`failed(err)`); the export route logged only a count, so the
  cause was nowhere. The helper now logs the cause with its step and returns fixed text; the route
  logs which parts failed (`errors`, fixed texts naming the part); `platform/auth/data-export.ts`
  logs each part's cause where it catches it.
- **The guard.** It scans all of `platform/`, `app/api` and `lib/` (baseline 0, so any new site
  fails), and follows a caught error into a helper that returns its text — the file's own
  (`failed(err)`, `errorText(err)`, `this.codedFailure(err, …)`), or one another scanned file
  exports and this one imports. A helper is a function whose parameter (untyped, `unknown`, `any` or
  an `Error` type) has its text leave by the same rules; one that only logs it is not. Run on the
  base trees it reports 138 sites in PF and 140 in Playform (the 118, the Cognito providers'
  `codedFailure`, review-service's `errorText`, provider-health's `errorMessage`, Playform's
  `failed(err)`); after this change, none.
- **R-75 (N-57) — screen literals.** After TASK-202: PF 232, Playform 270. Every one is in the
  catalog, in the pattern the screens already use — a module-local `t` over
  `renderMessage("screens.<area>.<key>")`: shared screens in `messages/en.json`
  (`screens.auth.{profile,page,login,register,forgot_password,new_password,age_gate,mfa_challenge,email_verification,layout,sso}`,
  `screens.admin_console.views`, `screens.review_dashboard`, `screens.adaptive_input`,
  `screens.appeal`, `screens.error_boundary`, `screens.home`); a repository's own screens in its
  `messages/app/en.json` under `screens.app` (PF: the spike page and the auth page client). The scan
  also missed a string a JSX expression shows or a label attribute's expression gives
  (`{busy ? "Saving..." : "Save"}`, `aria-label={on ? "Stop" : "Start"}`): 39 in PF, 50 in
  Playform; it counts them now, and they moved too. A sentence with a styled part (an address in
  white, an approver, a bold state) stays one message, and the part is placed where the translation

  member count is an ICU plural. English is the only locale (ADR-051 D6, `CATALOGS`), so English is
  each string's only translation. The guard requires 0 in both repositories and fails on any
  literal, by its place; a new check fails any catalog key a screen names that English does not
  have (a missing key renders as the key itself).
- **R-75, the rest — text that reaches a screen indirectly.** The scans above see a literal where
  the screen shows it; text kept elsewhere and shown through a name passed them by: the input's mode
  table (`MODE_CONFIG[mode].label`, `.ariaLabel`, `.title`) and its default placeholder, the
  sign-in providers' button labels, the profile's visibility options, the auth layout's default
  title and subtitle, the review queue's status filters, decisions and actions (shown as words: now
  from the catalog, in the same words, and the item's own status, decision and action with them),
  the entitlements table's headers and empty line, the capability map's panel name, the guest
  sign-in's failure and the review queue's connection failure, the dual-control panel's change
  comment, and each repository's page titles and descriptions (`metadata`). Each is in the catalog
  now; a language's name comes from `screens.app.languages` through `components/language-name.ts`
  (shared), never from a list in a component or the name an API answer carries.
  `section-hints.ts`'s "(unknown tool)" was never shown — a permission no one holds — and is now a
  code (`permission.unknown_tool`). A new guard, `__tests__/screen-text-indirect.test.ts`, at 0 in
  both repositories: rule A follows every name in a text position (a variable, a property chain,
  an alias, a `.map`/`.find` parameter, a default prop, a function's returned values, an import) to
  the literals it can hold; rule B reports words for a person anywhere in the screens' code (app/
  but its API routes, components/, hooks/, platform's .tsx) outside the catalog, a log, an error,
  a comparison or a technical attribute — text that reaches a screen through a prop or a hook's
  state. Code-shaped strings (CSS, cookies, dotted keys, paths, identifiers, ISO codes, HTTP
  methods) are not words. On the first pass's commits it reports 70 findings in PF and 150 in
  Playform (one literal both rules see is listed twice); now none. Rendered DOM equal to the base's
  in the screens it touched (335 PF and 451 Playform renders); the routed ones walked again,
  unchanged.

Walked: every routed screen whose text moved, on production builds of the base trees and of this
change, at 1280 px and 390 px — PF's sign-in, create-account, forgot-password and home (guest,
signed in), Playform's same plus the language picker, `/agent/console`, `/agent/authorize`, `/admin`
and its data views (roles, entitlements, password policy, approval policy, capabilities, capability
map, per-account), and the admin console spec's own walk (TASK-202). PF: 10 of 10 shots identical
pixel for pixel; Playform: 23 of 32 identical, 9 differ by 31–102 anti-aliased pixels where a
sentence that was several text nodes is now one run (no word, position or size changed). Screens
no route mounts (the profile page, the review dashboard, the adaptive input, the appeal form and
others) were compared by their rendered DOM in every one of their tests: 325 PF and 429 Playform
renders, none different.

Credits: MITRE's CWE-209, "Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information" (MITRE
Corporation), and the OWASP Error Handling Cheat Sheet (OWASP Foundation): a generic message to the
caller, the detail to the log.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** every caller of the changed platform functions — routes (account age, export, delete;
  the auth routes through the providers' results; `/api/health`; the admin and operator routes
  through audit, erasure, moderation and approvals records), the jobs (erasure retries, approval
  expiry), the relink command an operator runs, and the screens. No permission, guard or route
  changes who can call what.
- **Races:** none new: every change is in what a failure carries, after the failure. The relink
  command's chunks, the pipeline's claims and the erasure steps run as before; only their reason
  texts change.
- **Dependencies down:** this is the change's subject. Each dependency's failure still fails (or
  degrades) as before — the same status, the same refusal code, the same retry — and its cause is
  now in the log line at the catch, with the step, module, user or probe it concerns. A logger that
  throws is not new (the code already logged at most of these sites).
- **Erasure leftovers:** less is stored: an erasure's results, its external stores' outcomes and
  the audit log's failure reasons no longer copy a store's message (which could name an address or
  a value). Nothing new is stored.
- **Screens × responses:** responses keep their codes and statuses; the texts that change are
  fields people read: the audit log's failed-act reason (Audit log view), approvals'
  `lastRunError` (Approvals), erasure errors and external outcomes (Erasures), the moderation
  queue's restore and strike messages (review dashboard), health details (`/api/health`), the
  relink command's report lines (the operator's terminal), `AuthResult.error` (logs only: routes
  answer `errorCode`). The screens: every literal moved, rendered identically (above).
- **Journeys touched:** none changes path. Sign-in, sign-up, password reset, the home page as guest
  and user, the agent console and authorize page, the admin console's data views — walked, and
  Playform's E2E suite runs the same 25 specs with the same outcomes as on the base.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No. It removes a leak (a store's or provider's text into
  records and answers others read); refusals, codes, statuses and permissions are unchanged, and
  the screens' text is the same.

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** text crossing from a failed dependency (database, cache, Cognito, AI provider,
  speech and song providers, external erasure stores) into what the platform returns, stores or
  shows — results, records, health answers, screens.
- **Bypasses:** a site the guard cannot see — through a helper (now followed, same file or
  imported), a cast or a template (already), a `.catch` callback (already); a helper whose parameter
  is typed `string` is not followed (it cannot hold an error). Not followed: a caught error kept in a
  variable and read later outside the catch (`const e = err; … e.message`) — none exists; the guard's
  header says so.
- **Forgeries:** an actor who can make a dependency's error carry text — a user whose input is
  echoed in a provider's error, a database constraint naming a value they chose — could get it into
  an admin-visible record before; now it reaches only the log. Actors that exist today: users and
  guests of a deployment (their own input), tenants' administrators (records they read). No other
  actor is assumed.
- **Legitimate flows:** a failure is still reported, by code and fixed text, to the caller that
  handles it; the operator reads the cause in the log line (the relink command's own stderr, the
  deployment's logs); every screen shows the same words.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for batch 55e (2026-11-08: fix every site to a stable,
  safe code or message with the detail to the log only; baseline 0 and the guard failing on any new
  site; R-78's diagnostic restored; every screen literal into the catalog the repositories already
  use, baseline 0, walked at 1280 and 390 px). No commit precedes this entry; the owner reviews it
  with the change.

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** for each changed result field, its readers: the age route (now
  `errorCode`), the delete route (`users: no such user`, kept by type), the export route (logs
  `errors`), `hold-authority` and `tool-invoker` (`reason` into audit records — fixed text),
  `isStaleChangeFailure` (the stale code comes from `reportsFailure`, not a catch — unchanged),
  the relink report and its tests (stamp names kept), `authResultResponse` / `errorFromResult`
  (`error` reaches `internalError`'s log only), metrics readers (`ai_metrics.error` is a class now).
  The tests that asserted a dependency's raw text (25 files in each repository) now assert the
  fixed text and, where the reason mattered, that the cause was logged. The
  screens: every changed component's tests, unchanged, pass; their rendered DOM equals the base's.
- **Hostile re-read:** tried to get a database message into an erasure record (`users: …`, an
  external store's outcome — fixed texts, tests), into the audit log's reason (fixed — DB test),
  into a health answer (fixed — tests), into an approval's `lastRunError` (fixed — tests); to hide
  a site behind a local helper, an imported helper, a method helper (all reported by the guard's
  self-test); to make a `string` parameter's template count as error text (not reported —
  self-test); to break a key a screen uses (the key check fails, proven by renaming one); to change
  a shown number's grouping (kept as text; DOM equal); to hide a label in a table, an alias, a
  callback, a default prop, a function's return, an import, a component's prop, a hook's
  notification (each reported by the indirect guard's self-tests); to pass a CSS value, a cookie,
  a dotted key or an HTTP method off as words (not reported — self-test).

### TASK-203 — Erasure, retention, security and dual-control readiness

| Field        | Detail                                                                                                    |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ID**       | TASK-203                                                                                                  |
| **Type**     | Defect (erasure readiness, retention, dual control that could not be satisfied, input and record gaps)    |
| **Severity** | High (an erasure held for an approver who did not exist; rows kept with no limit; an unbounded purge)     |
| **Phase**    | Phase 5                                                                                                   |
| **Target**   | v6.0.0 (RC)                                                                                               |
| **Status**   | Fixed on develop (sub-batch 55c of the residuals batch); owner steps below                                |
| **Logged**   | 2026-11-08 (the rebuilt residuals register: N-22–N-29, N-31, N-35–N-37, N-52–N-56, N-83, N-85, N-87–N-91) |

**1. Dual control that nobody could satisfy (N-24, N-85).** Every dual-controlled action — an
erasure, a role change, a held setting, a catalog change, a tenant's deletion, an erasure's
attestation — waited for an approver who was not the requester, and nothing checked that one
existed: a deployment with one super_admin accepted an erasure, held it, and it lapsed while the
erasure deadline ran. The rules stay as strict as they were; what changed is when the answer comes:

- `platform/admin/eligible-approvers.ts` reads who could approve, as the permission engine resolves
  it (role, inherited role, active entitlement; an account in good standing), and the request path
  refuses up front, before anything is held: `approvals.no_eligible_approver` (409), naming the
  action and every permission its approver needs, when no account but the requester (and the
  account the action acts on) could approve it — the command bar and the screens on it (Users,
  Entitlements, the erasure route), held settings (`requestApproval`, the config tools), tenant
  deletion and erasure attestation. The action's own approver rule (a role change: every
  permission of both roles) is applied per account, the same function the decision runs. In a
  shared deployment an operator of any tenant counts for a tenant's hold (platform_operate and the
  approval's permissions), as the operators' approval routes allow. A read failure refuses
  (`service.unavailable`), never holds.
- Operator readiness gains a `dual_control` check (`platform/admin/dual-control-readiness.ts`):
  every dual-controlled action, per tenant with staff and across the deployment for operators'
  actions, that has no second eligible approver — named with what its approver needs.
- The users and entitlements routes answered every refused action as 503; a coded refusal is now
  answered with its own code.
- TENANCY_OPERATIONS "The second super admin": a guarded SQL block the owner runs once (tenant
  `default`; exactly one non-deleted account with the address; not already a super_admin; not the
  mailbox of an existing super_admin, `+tags` ignored; exactly one super_admin today), with its
  `role_bootstrap` audit record and the check queries — every column checked against the
  migrations (`last_login_at`, not `last_sign_in_at`), and run as written against the replayed
  schema by `__tests__/db/second-super-admin.db.test.ts` (each refusal too). It joins the documented
  hand-edit exceptions (CLAUDE.md, `review-process` guard).

**2. Erasure readiness (N-22, N-23, N-52, N-54, N-55).** Operator readiness gains `erasure`: with
the administrative key, DescribeUserPool must answer this pool, ListUsers is allowed (a lookup of a
name no pool user can have) and AdminDeleteUser is allowed (its delete of that absent name answers
`UserNotFoundException`; it is never sent when the lookup found someone) — a refusal names the
action and the policy. The administrative key is needed in every tenancy mode (erasure deletes
identities with it); the contract's hint, ENV_REFERENCE and TENANCY_OPERATIONS §3.3 name the inline
policy `cognito-tenancy-and-erasure` and its eight actions, scoped to the one pool, from one list
(`COGNITO_ADMIN_ACTIONS`) that a test holds to every action the provider sends. **N-52, decided:**
`client_secret` compares the app client's secret (DescribeUserPoolClient) with
`COGNITO_CLIENT_SECRET` in constant time, on demand from the readiness page — never a sign-in, never
periodic, never the secret in an answer (TASK-197 residual 3). The pool is proven at erase time too
when the soft delete could not prove it (throttled, not yet permitted), from the same
`user_deletions.cognito_sub` the erase uses (TASK-193 residuals).

**3. Retention (N-25, N-26).** `platform/jobs/retention.ts` answers for every platform table: a rule
(its age, what happens, who applies it) or why it is kept, and
`__tests__/db/retention-coverage.db.test.ts` fails on a table of the schema with no entry (an app's
own tables in its manifest's `retention`). The rules no other duty applied run in the new
`data.retention` job, every tenant, suspended ones too: audit and consent rows lose their IP address
and user agent after `retention.network_identifiers_days` (90); interactions, AI metrics,
content-safety decisions (not one a strike rests on), resolved effects, idle guests, idle sessions
and past budget counters are deleted after their own `retention.*` age — each a governed,
operator-only, bounded setting (migration 064). The trajectory-retention job and the new job are
dual-controlled (`config.dual_control_keys`, seeded once as 052 seeded its keys).

**4. The purge (N-27, N-28, N-29).** A purge that ran out of time reported `failed` while its step
could still complete; now it is `indeterminate` (purge_log, 064), the step's signal is aborted, each
step reported as not known or not started, a late completion logged, and the account stays due. A
refused or failed erasure request left its `attempted` record open; it is closed `refused` with the
code, and an alert (`gdpr.request_record_unclosed`) when even that cannot be written. The cache and
rate-limit purge handlers no pipeline ran are removed, and with them the AI cache's whole-cache
clear and `purgeUserData` (it keys by prompt, not by person).

**5. Inputs and records (N-31, N-37, N-56).** Every JSON body is read against its schema
(`body-schema-baseline.json` at zero; the guard now fails on any schemaless read). Bodies whose part
is an action's input read it against the keys some action's schema names, a setting's value as a
configuration value (`CONFIG_VALUE_SCHEMA`, held to every seeded value by a DB test); a key the
server sets is refused `request.field_not_accepted` at any depth (`readJsonBody`'s `notAccepted`
paths). Claiming and releasing a moderation case are audited (`review_claimed` /
`review_unclaimed`); with no record, nothing changes. `tenant.invalid` echoes at most 100
characters, control characters removed.

**6. Migrations (N-53, N-87).** Migration 064 makes `applied_migrations` refuse recording a
migration older than one already recorded unless the session names it
(`platform.migration_reapply`); the replay checks the refusal and the deliberate re-apply
(TASK-197 residual 1). TENANCY_OPERATIONS "Reconciling the migration record": a guarded procedure to
retire a record whose file no branch has, or record a file applied without one, with its audit
record (tested as written). `migration-parity.mjs --records-may-lead` lists records ahead of a
branch as information.

**7. Security debt (N-35, N-36, N-83).** SEC-001 resolved (stale); SEC-012 and SEC-013 traced with `npm ls` (dev and build only: jest's
coverage chain and ESLint's; `--omit=dev` lists neither; no import), kept accepted with the
evidence; H-13 stays accepted with its reason written; TASK-044's state and owner steps recorded.

**8. What this batch found, fixed in it (the coordinator's ruling: no residuals).**

- **SEC-017, styles without `'unsafe-inline'`.** `style-src 'self' 'nonce-…'`: Next.js puts the
  request's nonce on the tags it renders — the approach of the Next.js documentation's "Content
  Security Policy" guide (nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/content-security-policy, Vercel). The two
  components that rendered `style` attributes no longer do (ErrorBoundary: classes; the review
  dashboard's confidence bar: its width set on the element's style object from script, which the
  policy allows); `no-inline-style-attributes` refuses a new one (JSX or `setAttribute("style")`).
  Playform's `e2e/csp.spec.ts` checks the header and that the sign-in page, the main page and the
  admin console (each section opened) raise no CSP violation, with a planted un-nonced style seen
  as one. SEC-017 resolved.
- **npm audit.** Before, in both repositories: 33 (4 low, 29 moderate) — glob (GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4),
  minimatch (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249), qs (four advisories), deepmerge (CVE-2026-93753), and what
  depends on them, `@sentry/nextjs` on the production path. Upgrades: `@sentry/nextjs` 11.11.0 (its
  bundler plugins take glob ^14.0.3), `@stryker-mutator/core` 10.1.1. Where upstream has no fix,
  overrides, each in the Dependency Overrides register with its reason and removal condition: glob
  ^14.0.4 (jest 30.5.2, test-exclude), minimatch ^11.0.5 under Stryker, test-exclude and
  typescript-estree, qs ^6.17.1 (Stryker's typed-rest-client pins 6.15.1), and deepmerge — no fixed
  release exists — as `vendor/deepmerge`, 4.3.1's build with each key written as an own property
  (MIT, its authors credited; `vendored-deepmerge` shows the poisoning on upstream's assignment and
  not on ours). After: `npm audit` and `npm audit --omit=dev` find 0, in both.
- **The tenants table at 390 px** scrolled the whole page (74 px): the operator console's three
  tables now scroll inside their own box, as the console's lists do (TASK-202).
- **Playform's expired delegation requests** are deleted by age (Playform TASK-5004).

**Owner steps** (in order; each with its check). (1) Apply migration 064 in the SQL Editor; check
`select filename from applied_migrations where filename like '064%';` (one row) and
`select key from platform_config where key like 'retention.%' order by 1;` (eight keys). (2) Give
every deployment's Cognito key the inline policy `cognito-tenancy-and-erasure` (TENANCY_OPERATIONS
§3.3) and open the operator readiness page: `erasure` and `client_secret` ready. (3) If readiness
names actions with no second approver, add a second super admin with the procedure in
TENANCY_OPERATIONS (the person signs in once first). (4) After deploy, run `data.retention` from
the jobs page, or wait a day. (5) Run `npm ci` after pulling: the lockfile changed (overrides, the
vendored deepmerge).

**Playform.** The same shared files byte for byte; its own Cognito readiness checks, retention for
its tables, credential register and env reference (N-89, N-90), LIVE_JOURNEY_CHECK §8 (N-91) and the
parity workflow (N-87) — Playform TASK-5004 in `docs/PLAYFORM_TASKS.md`.

**Design check**

- **Reach:** the erasure route, the Users and Entitlements screens, the command bar, the config
  assistant and settings (a request no one else could approve is now refused, coded, not held);
  every route body (a key no schema names is refused); operator readiness (three checks); the
  purge pipeline and the erasure job; a new daily job; migration 064. Guests and agents: no change
  except through these routes.
- **Races:** the approver read is a snapshot: an approver removed after a request is held leaves it
  held, as before (expiry ends it). Retention deletes in batches of 5000 by `ctid` in its own
  transactions; a row written meanwhile is younger than the cutoff. The migration trigger runs in
  the inserting transaction.
- **Dependencies down:** the staff read failing refuses the request (`service.unavailable`); a
  Cognito check that cannot answer is `unknown`, never ready; a purge step past its time limit is
  `indeterminate`.
- **Erasure leftovers:** none added: the readiness probe names no person; retention removes more.
- **Screens × responses:** the readiness panel lists the three new checks; a refused request shows
  its coded message (en.json) wherever a held one showed "held".
- **Journeys touched:** none exempted or added.
- **Weakens a tenant's protection?** No: no approval rule is relaxed; an operator counting as an
  approver is the rule the operators' routes already applied.

**Threat model**

- **Boundary:** the admin and operator routes, the request bodies, the erasure pipeline, the
  migration record. The actors that exist: the owner (the only account with 2FA that merges and the
  only operator today), staff accounts of the deployment (super_admin, admin, safety_approver,
  moderator) and ordinary users; the owner's AI agent working on the code; AWS Cognito; Supabase.
- **Bypasses** (our own mistakes): an erasure accepted and left to lapse (refused up front now); a
  setting or role change accepted with no possible approver (same); a body key nobody declared
  reaching a stored payload (refused); a migration re-applied out of order by hand in the SQL
  Editor (refused unless named); a purge reported failed while its step completed (indeterminate);
  a claim of another account's case leaving no record (audited).
- **Forgeries:** none in scope: each needs an actor who does not exist (a second operator account,
  a forged Cognito answer); not a residual.
- **Legitimate flows:** an erasure, role change or held setting in a tenant with a second eligible
  admin (held, as before); an operator deciding a tenant's hold; the readiness page read by the
  owner; the first super admin's bootstrap (ADR-013) and the documented procedures.
- **Agreed before code:** the owner's brief for sub-batch 55c (2026-11-08): refuse up front with a
  clear message, rules stay strict; readiness names each unapprovable action; the second super
  admin procedure; N-52 decided and recorded.

**Self-review**

- **Consumers checked:** every caller of `requestApproval`, `runCommandBarAction`,
  `requestTenantDeletion`, `requestErasureAttestation`; every `readJsonObject`/`readJsonBody`
  (`body-schema-baseline.json` to zero); every reader of `PurgeStatus` and purge_log.status
  (`status-lifecycle` register classifies `indeterminate`); every import of the removed handlers
  and `clearAll`; every test tenant that held a change with one admin (given a second approver, or
  asserting the refusal where the rules let no one approve — a super_admin's own role, erasure).
- **Hostile re-read:** tried a requester's id in another case, subject or address as the only
  approver (excluded — test); an approver suspended until tomorrow, a restriction that ended, a
  deleted account, an entitlement (DB test); the target as the only approver (refused); a server
  key nested in a plan's second action (refused with its path — test); a pool user named like the
  probe (the delete never sent — test); a delete that succeeds, another pool, a throttled pool
  (never ready — test); the second-super-admin block with the placeholder, a second account with
  the address, a `+tag` of the first super admin's mailbox, two super admins already (each refused,
  as written in the document — test); a retention rule deleting a strike's decision (kept — test);
  an inline style without the nonce on the sign-in page (refused and reported — the CSP spec's
  self-test), a `style` attribute in JSX or set with `setAttribute` (the guard's self-test), a
  parsed `__proto__` key through the vendored deepmerge as target, source, or into a
  null-prototype object (prototype untouched — test), `npm ci` from the new lockfile (installs,
  `npm ls` clean).
